The PAPACY is an active third party: the Pope tracks each Catholic faction's standing, demands ceasefires, calls CRUSADES against named cities that any faction may join for prestige and cheap fervent troops, and EXCOMMUNICATES rulers who ignore him — stripping them of protection and inviting attack — while a faction with enough cardinals can influence who becomes Pope. Mirror it with jihads for Islamic factions. Add agents with real economic roles: merchants who occupy a resource on the map to earn from it and can attempt to acquire a rival merchant's business, priests who spread religion and suppress heresy, princesses who marry into other dynasties for alliances, and assassins and spies. Let settlements branch into either a CITY oriented on trade and population or a CASTLE oriented on military recruitment, a choice that shapes the empire. Span the gunpowder transition so late armies play differently from early ones.
prompts.watchFor: Only one of the two layers; battles decided by hit-point attrition with no morale or routing; the Pope as a flavour message with no excommunication, crusades or cardinal politics; agents reduced to spies with no merchants, priests or marriage diplomacy; settlements with a single upgrade path rather than the city and castle branch; gunpowder units that are just stronger archers; no siege equipment or wall assaults.

prompts.title: Titan Quest
prompts.prompt: Build Titan Quest as a multi-file web isometric action RPG set in the real mythologies of Greece, Egypt and China, following actual geography and legend rather than invented fantasy. There are no fixed classes; instead the player picks a MASTERY at level two and a SECOND MASTERY at level eight, and the pair IS the class — with a distinct name for every combination — so the build decision is a permanent branching choice made twice, and the two trees must be usable together in ways that create real hybrids rather than one carrying the other. Structure each mastery tree so that skills come in two kinds: active abilities on a tier gated by mastery investment, and PASSIVE MODIFIERS that hang beneath a specific active skill and reshape it — adding a chain, a burn, a knockback, extra projectiles — so points spent under a skill change how it behaves rather than just increasing a number. Add a loot system with randomised affixes, set items with graduated bonuses that unlock as more pieces are worn, and CHARMS and RELICS that are socketed into equipment and can be completed by finding further copies for a bonus effect. Include reserved-energy auras, pets that scale off skills, and a difficulty ladder that replays the campaign at higher monster levels with resistance penalties.
prompts.watchFor: Fixed classes instead of two chosen masteries; a second mastery that unlocks late enough to be irrelevant or that shares the first tree; skill trees with only rank-up numbers and no passive modifiers attached beneath skills; a hand-written drop table instead of rolled affixes; sets with a single all-or-nothing bonus; charms and relics missing or non-completable; generic fantasy monsters in place of specific mythological ones.

prompts.title: Garry's Mod
prompts.prompt: Build Garry's Mod as a multi-file web physics sandbox using three.js for rendering and a real rigid-body physics engine for simulation (both vendored locally). There is no goal, no score and no win condition, and that is deliberate — the deliverable is a toolkit. Build the PHYSGUN first: a beam that grabs any dynamic object in the world at range, holds it at a distance the player can push and pull, rotates it freely while held, and FREEZES it in place on command so it becomes static scaffolding. Then build the TOOL GUN, whose tools are the actual game and which must include real constraint types, because contraptions come from constraints: weld to fuse two props rigidly, rope and elastic with adjustable length and stiffness, axis and ball-socket to create hinges and joints, wheel with a driven axle bound to a key, thruster bound to a key with adjustable force, hydraulic that extends and retracts on a key, and balloon with lift. The acceptance test is that a player can weld a chassis, attach four wheels on axes, bind them to the arrow keys and DRIVE the result — a working vehicle built entirely from generic props and constraints, with nothing vehicle-specific in the code. Add a spawn menu of props, ragdolls that can be posed and constrained, an undo stack, and a duplicator that copies a whole contraption.
prompts.watchFor: A prop spawner with no constraint tools, which makes contraptions impossible; welds that parent objects rather than creating a physical constraint; no key binding on thrusters, wheels or hydraulics, so nothing can be controlled; a physgun that cannot rotate or freeze; prebuilt vehicles supplied instead of emerging from constraints; no undo or duplicator; objects that are kinematic rather than genuinely simulated.

prompts.title: Portal
prompts.prompt: Build Portal as a multi-file web first-person puzzle game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons). The player carries a device that places exactly two linked portals — one orange, one blue — onto surfaces flagged as portalable, and anything entering one instantly emerges from the other. Two properties make this a mechanic rather than a teleporter, and both are required. First, RECURSIVE RENDERING: looking through a portal must show the view from the other portal, including the player's own body and including further portal views nested several levels deep, rendered live rather than faked with a static texture. Second, MOMENTUM CONSERVATION: velocity is preserved through the transition and rotated into the exit portal's frame, so falling a long way into a portal on the floor and out of one on a wall converts that fall speed into a horizontal LAUNCH — 'speedy thing goes in, speedy thing comes out' — and flinging is the basis of the late puzzles. Build the test-chamber progression as a teaching curve that introduces weighted cubes, floor buttons, energy pellets, turrets that can be toppled or portalled, emancipation grids that strip carried objects and close portals, and goo. Let an unseen narrator comment continuously on the player's performance with increasingly untrustworthy cheerfulness, and break the chambers open into the machinery behind them.
prompts.watchFor: Portals rendered as a flat texture or a fade instead of a live recursive view; momentum discarded or reset on transit, which deletes every flinging puzzle; portals placeable on any surface with no material restriction; carried objects passing through emancipation grids; puzzles solvable without portals; the narrator absent or reduced to hint text; no escape from the test chambers into the facility behind them.

prompts.title: BioShock
prompts.prompt: Build BioShock as a multi-file web first-person immersive sim using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), set in a flooded, art-deco undersea city whose ideology visibly failed. Combat is TWO-HANDED and that is the design: a conventional weapon in the right hand and a PLASMID power in the left, used together in the same moment. The plasmids must interact with the ENVIRONMENT as a reagent system, which is the acceptance test — electricity discharged into a puddle of water must stun everything standing in it, an incinerate must ignite spilled oil into a spreading fire, freezing an enemy standing in water must lock them solid, and telekinesis must let the player catch an incoming grenade or rocket in mid-air and throw it back. Add security cameras, turrets and bots that can be HACKED and turned against their owners, and a wrench for the desperate. Tell the entire history of the city through AUDIO DIARIES scattered in the world, playable while the player keeps moving, with no cutscenes. Put a recurring moral choice at the centre — the Little Sisters, who can be harvested for immediate power or rescued for less now and more later — and let the accumulated pattern of those choices select the ending. Include a late narrative reveal that reframes the player's own obedience throughout the game.
prompts.watchFor: Plasmids as elemental damage types that never interact with water, oil or the world; no two-handed layout, with powers occupying a weapon slot; hacking that simply disables a device instead of turning it to your side; audio diaries replaced by cutscenes or by text the player must stand still to read; the Little Sister choice with no effect on the ending; the reveal delivered without any mechanical grounding in how the player has actually been playing.

prompts.title: Crysis
prompts.prompt: Build Crysis as a multi-file web first-person shooter using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), across large open jungle-island levels rather than corridors. The NANOSUIT is the whole game and its design must be preserved exactly: four modes — Armour, Strength, Speed and Cloak — that all draw from ONE SHARED ENERGY POOL which drains while a mode is exerted and recharges only when the suit is idle in the default state. That single pool is the acceptance test, because it forces a constant economy: cloak across the open ground and arrive with no energy left for armour, or sprint in loud and fast and have nothing left to absorb the first burst. Strength must apply to more than punching — higher jumps, steadier aim, harder melee, and further grenade throws. Build objectives that can be approached from any direction across genuinely open terrain, so the player can scout with binoculars, tag enemies, and choose between a silent cloaked infiltration, a vehicle assault, or bringing down the trees and huts around a patrol. Make the environment reactive: palm trees that fall when shot or driven through, huts and shacks that break apart, and foliage that physically parts. Add drivable jeeps, boats and armour, a weapon customisation system for attachments applied in the field, and enemies who flank and call reinforcements.
prompts.watchFor: Separate cooldowns or separate meters per suit mode, which removes the economy that makes the suit interesting; energy that recharges while a mode is active; strength mode limited to melee; linear corridor levels that defeat the multiple-approach design; static indestructible jungle; vehicles as scripted sequences; weapon attachments locked to a menu between missions rather than swappable in the field.

prompts.title: Team Fortress 2
prompts.prompt: Build Team Fortress 2 as a multi-file web class-based multiplayer shooter using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), with a stylised illustrated look where every class is instantly readable by SILHOUETTE, colour and stance — the art direction is a gameplay system, since a player must identify a threat and its counter at a glance across a map. prompts.watchFor: Classes that share a weapon pool and differ only in numbers; silhouettes too similar to identify at range; a Medic who heals without building an Übercharge; an Engineer whose buildings cannot be upgraded, repaired or destroyed; a Spy with disguise but no per-class appearance or no positional backstab; no class counters, so one class dominates; a single game mode; no setup phase.

prompts.title: The Witcher
prompts.prompt: Build The Witcher as a multi-file web role-playing game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), in a grimy, politically ugly fantasy world where the protagonist is a professional monster killer distrusted by everyone. The moral design is the point and must be built structurally: significant choices offer no clean option, the game never signals which is good, and — the acceptance test — the CONSEQUENCES ARE DELAYED, surfacing chapters later as changed factions, dead or living characters, and closed or opened questlines, long after the player can connect them to the decision or reload past it. Build PREPARATION as the combat system: potions are toxic and can only be drunk BEFORE a fight during meditation, never mid-combat, they are brewed from ingredients harvested from specific monster corpses and herbs, and they carry a toxicity budget that limits how many can be active. Pair that with a BESTIARY the player must actually read — filled in by reading books and questioning locals — which is where a monster's vulnerability, the right oil for the blade and the right sign are learned. prompts.watchFor: Choices with an obviously good option, or consequences that resolve immediately in the same scene; potions drinkable during combat, which removes all preparation; alchemy ingredients bought from a vendor rather than harvested; a bestiary that auto-fills and is never needed; silver and steel swords interchangeable; combat as free-swing hack and slash with no stance selection or rhythm timing; a morality meter.

prompts.title: Left 4 Dead
prompts.prompt: Build Left 4 Dead as a multi-file web four-player co-operative shooter using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons). The system that makes it more than a horde shooter is the AI DIRECTOR, and it must be a real feedback controller rather than a random spawner: continuously measure each survivor's stress from health, recent damage taken, ammunition, time since the last threat and distance travelled, aggregate it into a tension value, and then actively SHAPE the level in response — withholding enemies to build a lull, releasing a horde at the peak, placing special infected ahead of the group, and positioning health kits, pills and ammo where the team's condition warrants. The acceptance test is that two runs of the same campaign map must produce measurably different spawn counts, item placements and horde timings driven by measured player state, not by a seed. Build four special infected that each DISABLE a survivor in a way only a teammate can undo — a tongue that drags a survivor away, a pounce that pins one to the ground, a bile attack that blinds and attracts the entire horde, and a giant that hurls concrete and survivors — so the team must stay together or lose members one by one. prompts.watchFor: A random or seeded spawner presented as a director, with no measurement of player state; identical horde timing and item placement across runs; specials that simply do damage instead of pinning a survivor who requires rescue; no friendly fire, which removes the cost of poor discipline; downed players who self-revive; a campaign that plays identically solo, so the co-operative dependency never bites; no Versus mode.

prompts.title: Fallout 3
prompts.prompt: Build Fallout 3 as a multi-file web open-world role-playing game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), carrying the SPECIAL attributes, skills and perks of the isometric originals into a first-person ruined city. The bridge between the two forms is V.A.T.S., and it is the acceptance test: at any moment the player freezes the real-time action into a targeting mode, spends ACTION POINTS to queue shots at specific BODY PARTS — head, torso, arms, legs, weapon — each showing an honest computed hit percentage derived from distance, cover, weapon condition and the relevant skill, then watches the queue resolve on a slow cinematic camera with crippling effects applied per limb. It must be a genuine alternative to free aiming, not a slow-motion aim assist. Build the world as a hand-crafted ruin that rewards EXPLORATION over quest-following: metro tunnels connecting surface districts, vaults with their own self-contained stories told through terminals and audio logs, and dense environmental storytelling in places no quest sends you. prompts.watchFor: V.A.T.S. as a slow-motion mode with no action-point cost, no per-body-part targeting or no honest hit percentages; crippled limbs with no behavioural effect; a procedurally generated wasteland instead of hand-authored ruins; locations that exist only as quest destinations; weapons that never degrade; radiation folded into ordinary damage; karma with no faction reaction; a single ending.

prompts.title: Dead Space
prompts.prompt: Build Dead Space as a multi-file web survival horror game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), aboard a derelict mining ship. Two systems define it and both must be built exactly. First, STRATEGIC DISMEMBERMENT: enemies do not die from body or head shots — the only way to stop one is to SEVER ITS LIMBS, and which limbs are cut changes its behaviour, so shooting the legs off drops a creature that then crawls fast along the floor, taking the arms off removes its attack but not its charge, and severed parts remain as physical objects. Aiming becomes a resource problem because ammunition is scarce and body shots are waste. Second, a fully DIEGETIC INTERFACE: there is no HUD overlay anywhere. Health is a glowing spine on the back of the player's suit, stasis charge sits beside it, ammunition counts are holograms projected from the weapon itself, and the inventory, map and audio logs are holograms projected into world space IN FRONT of the character while the game continues running around them — opening the inventory must NOT pause the world, which is the acceptance test that the UI is genuinely in the fiction. Add stasis to slow a target briefly, kinesis to pick up and fire severed limbs and objects as weapons, zero-gravity sections with directional jumps between surfaces, and vacuum areas with a finite air supply.
prompts.watchFor: Enemies killed by conventional damage with dismemberment as a visual effect; limb loss that does not change behaviour; any 2D HUD overlay for health, ammo or objectives; an inventory that pauses the game; a mini-map or objective marker drawn on screen rather than projected in world space; unlimited ammunition; zero-gravity reduced to low gravity; no air supply in vacuum.

prompts.title: Spore
prompts.prompt: Build Spore as a multi-file web evolution simulation using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), spanning stages from a single cell to a galactic civilisation. The technical heart, and the acceptance test for the whole build, is the CREATURE EDITOR with PROCEDURAL RIGGING: the player stretches a spine, then attaches mouths, eyes, limbs, feet, hands, wings and details anywhere on it at any scale and in any number, and the game must automatically generate a skeleton and ANIMATE whatever they built — a creature with five legs of unequal length must work out a gait, a creature with none must slither, and a shared library of animations (walk, run, attack, dance, sing) must retarget onto arbitrary morphology at runtime. No preset skeletons and no fixed limb counts. The parts must feed back into the simulation as statistics: mouth type determines diet, feet determine speed, hands determine grasping, and the combination sets combat and social ability. Then build the stages as genuinely different genres sharing that creature — a 2D cell stage of eating and avoiding, a third-person creature stage of foraging, fighting and socialising to gain parts, a tribal real-time strategy stage, a civilisation stage of vehicles and city planning, and a space stage of exploring and terraforming a procedural galaxy — with each stage's outcome shaping the next.
prompts.watchFor: A creature editor limited to preset body plans, fixed limb counts or preset skeletons; animation that breaks or is skipped for unusual morphology; parts that are cosmetic and do not affect diet, speed or combat; stages that are all the same game with different art; stage outcomes that do not carry forward; a hand-authored galaxy rather than a procedural one; an editor whose creations cannot actually be played.

prompts.title: S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Clear Sky
prompts.prompt: Build S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Clear Sky as a multi-file web survival shooter using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), in a bleak irradiated exclusion zone of connected open maps. The system this entry is built around is FACTION WARS: several armed factions hold territory across the Zone and fight each other CONTINUOUSLY WITHOUT THE PLAYER — squads spawn, march to contested bases, assault them, take losses, capture or lose ground, and request reinforcements — so the territorial map genuinely shifts over time. The player may join a faction and take assignments that tip that ongoing war, and the acceptance test is that leaving the game running with the player idle must still produce a changed front line. Build ANOMALIES as invisible physics hazards detected by throwing bolts and by a handheld detector's rising tone, which conceal ARTIFACTS that grant a real bonus paired with a real cost, usually radiation the player must then treat with vodka, medkits or an anti-rad drug. Weapons and armour DEGRADE with use, jam when worn, and must be repaired by a technician for money, so gear is a running expense. Add hunger and sleep, a night that is genuinely dark and needs a torch, blowouts that force the player to reach shelter within a countdown, and trading with stalkers who will also just shoot you.
prompts.watchFor: Faction territory that only changes when the player completes a quest; squads that spawn on approach rather than existing and moving independently; anomalies made visible or harmless; artifacts with a bonus and no cost; weapons that never jam or degrade; no repair economy; nights that are lit well enough not to need a torch; blowouts as a cutscene with no shelter requirement.

prompts.title: Dragon Age: Origins
prompts.prompt: Build Dragon Age: Origins as a multi-file web party role-playing game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), returning to real-time-with-pause tactical combat over a party of four with a pull-back tactical camera. Two systems must be built. First, the ORIGINS themselves: six genuinely different opening chapters determined by the player's race, class and background — a noble's betrayal, an elf in an alienage, a mage in a tower, a dwarf commoner in the underclass — each a distinct playable prologue in a distinct location with its own cast, and each leaving a permanent mark that the rest of the game recognises, so NPCs, dialogue options and whole side quests differ hours later depending on where the character came from. Second, and the acceptance test for the combat system, the TACTICS editor: each companion has a list of programmable IF-THEN rules the player authors and orders by priority — 'if ally health below 25 percent, use healing spell', 'if enemy is casting, interrupt', 'if self surrounded by three or more, use area attack' — with conditions, targets and abilities chosen from real dropdowns, and slots that unlock with level, so the player is literally programming their party's autonomy. prompts.watchFor: A single shared opening with the origin reduced to a backstory line; origins that never affect later dialogue or quests; the tactics system absent, or reduced to preset behaviour modes like aggressive and defensive instead of a player-authored rule list; rules with no priority ordering; combat that cannot be paused and queued; companion approval with no effect on quests; choices that all resolve cleanly.

prompts.title: Left 4 Dead 2
prompts.prompt: Build Left 4 Dead 2 as a multi-file web four-player co-operative shooter using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), keeping the stress-measuring AI Director and extending its authority. The Director must now also reshape the LEVEL and the WEATHER, not just the population: alternate routes opening and closing between runs, and a storm sequence that rolls in dynamically to cut visibility to a few metres and force the team into a slow, blind, huddled crawl while the horde is unaffected. Add MELEE WEAPONS as real swung geometry with arcs, reach and stagger — a machete, a fire axe, a cricket bat, a frying pan — that cost nothing in ammunition but demand spacing, changing the economy of a fight. Extend the specials so each one CONTROLS a survivor differently rather than just damaging: one charges in a straight line and carries a survivor away while bowling over everyone in the path, one rides a survivor and steers them off the group, and one leaves a spreading pool of acid that denies ground and forces the team to move. prompts.watchFor: A Director that only spawns enemies and never alters routes or weather; the storm as a static lighting filter rather than a dynamic event that changes play; melee weapons as instant-hit attacks with no arc, reach or stagger; new specials that duplicate the old ones' pin behaviour; ammunition upgrades that are just a damage number; defibrillators that work like normal revives; Realism mode identical to the default.

prompts.title: League of Legends
prompts.prompt: Build a playable web slice of League of Legends as a multi-file game: one three-lane map, a jungle between the lanes, and a modest champion roster, built so the actual competitive systems are intact. Waves of AI MINIONS spawn on a timer from each base and walk their lane, fighting whatever they meet, and the single most important mechanic is LAST-HITTING — a champion earns gold only from dealing the KILLING BLOW to a minion, and gets nothing for damaging it, so the entire early game is a contest of precise timing against an opponent doing the same thing while denying you space. Towers deal escalating damage and must not be dived carelessly, and they only change target under specific aggro rules that players learn to exploit. Between the lanes put a JUNGLE of neutral camps that a dedicated jungler farms for experience and gold before ambushing lanes from the fog, plus two major neutral objectives that grant lasting team-wide buffs and are the reason teams fight at set times. Make progression HORIZONTAL: gold and levels are earned and spent entirely within a single match and reset at the end, so no player enters a match stronger than another. Give each champion a passive and four abilities on cooldowns and mana, and cover the map in fog of war lifted by placed wards.
prompts.watchFor: Gold awarded for damaging minions rather than for the last hit, which erases the core skill; minions that do not push lanes on their own; towers as scenery with no aggro rules or damage ramp; an empty jungle or neutral objectives with no team-wide buff; persistent between-match power progression that makes matches unequal; no fog of war or no wards; abilities without cooldowns or mana costs.

prompts.title: Batman: Arkham Asylum
prompts.prompt: Build Batman: Arkham Asylum as a multi-file web action-adventure using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons). Two combat modes, kept strictly separate, define it. FREEFLOW is for unarmed crowds and works as a rhythm system on essentially three inputs: strike, which automatically travels the player to ANY enemy in any direction with no target locking, counter, which must be pressed in response to a clear telegraphed prompt above an attacker about to hit, and evade. A COMBO MULTIPLIER climbs with every uninterrupted successful action and resets the instant the player is hit or whiffs, so the goal is unbroken flow rather than damage, and special moves unlock at combo thresholds. PREDATOR mode is for rooms of armed guards who will kill Batman in seconds in a straight fight: the player works from gargoyles and vents above, silently removing guards one at a time, and the survivors must visibly ESCALATE — checking corners, calling names, pairing up, shooting at shadows, panicking with rising heart rate and audible fear — so the room becomes psychologically different as it empties. Add Detective Vision as a toggled world view, gadgets that double as TRAVERSAL tools unlocking earlier areas, and an interconnected asylum that is backtracked through as new gadgets arrive.
prompts.watchFor: Combat with target lock-on or attacks that do not auto-travel to any enemy; a counter with no telegraph or one that can be spammed; a combo counter that survives being hit; predator rooms winnable by open combat; guards whose behaviour does not escalate as their number falls; gadgets that unlock nothing in the world, removing the backtracking; a level structure of disconnected missions instead of one interconnected asylum.

prompts.title: Minecraft (Early Access)
prompts.prompt: Build the early survival Minecraft as a multi-file web voxel game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons) — the survival loop specifically, not a creative building toy. Generate effectively endless terrain procedurally from noise into chunks with biomes, ore distributed by depth, and cave systems carved beneath, meshed with face culling so it stays fast. The mechanic that must be built properly is the SPATIAL CRAFTING GRID: recipes are PATTERNS on a three-by-three grid, not a list of ingredients, so a pickaxe is three planks across the top with two sticks down the middle and putting the same items in a different arrangement produces nothing — the player discovers recipes as shapes. Chain that into TOOL TIERS as a hard gate: wooden tools mine stone, stone tools mine iron ore, iron tools mine diamond, and no tier can skip ahead, which turns the whole early game into a forced descent. Add a furnace that smelts ore into ingots and cooks food over fuel with real time cost. Run a day/night cycle where light level is computed and propagated through the world, hostile mobs spawn in darkness and burn in daylight, so the first night is a genuine emergency that forces the player to dig in or build shelter. Track health and hunger, with falling, drowning, lava and mobs as real threats.
prompts.watchFor: A creative mode with unlimited blocks and no survival pressure; crafting as a flat recipe list with no spatial pattern; tool tiers that can be skipped so diamonds are reachable immediately; no light-level propagation, so caves and shelters are not actually dark; mobs that spawn regardless of light or that ignore daylight; no hunger or health; finite flat terrain with no chunking; rendering every block face instead of culling hidden ones.

prompts.title: StarCraft II: Wings of Liberty
prompts.prompt: Build StarCraft II: Wings of Liberty as a multi-file web real-time strategy game keeping the three genuinely asymmetric production models — Terran builders who stay with a structure and repair, Zerg larvae and creep, Protoss warp-in under pylon power with regenerating shields — and adding the layer this sequel introduced. Each race gets a distinct MACRO ABILITY on its town hall that converts player attention directly into economy, and these must be built because they are what separates a good player from a fast one: Terran orbital command drops a MULE, a temporary extra harvester that mines at high rate for a short life, or scans a fogged area; Protoss nexus casts Chrono Boost to accelerate one structure's production or research for a duration; Zerg queens inject a hatchery to spawn a batch of extra larvae on a timer that must be re-cast to keep unit production saturated. Modernise the interface honestly: unlimited unit selection, control groups, smart-casting that distributes an ability across selected casters rather than stacking it on one target, and rally points onto minerals. Build a campaign where between missions the player spends earned credits in an armoury on permanent unit upgrades and hires mercenaries, so the campaign has its own progression, and add a ladder skirmish mode with league placement.
prompts.watchFor: No per-race macro abilities, which removes the attention economy this entry is built on; MULEs, Chrono Boost or larva inject present but automatic rather than manually cast on a cooldown; smart-casting that stacks every selected caster's ability on one target; unit selection still capped at twelve; a campaign that is a mission list with no between-mission upgrade purchasing; three races sharing one production pipeline.

prompts.title: Fallout: New Vegas
prompts.prompt: Build Fallout: New Vegas as a multi-file web open-world role-playing game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), keeping SPECIAL, skills, perks and V.A.T.S., and building the reactivity systems it is actually celebrated for. FACTION REPUTATION is the spine and it must be TWO-AXIS: every faction tracks FAME and INFAMY as SEPARATE accumulating values rather than one slider, so a player can be simultaneously famous and infamous with the same faction and receive the mixed reception that follows — this is the acceptance test, and collapsing it into one number breaks the design. Reputation must gate greetings, prices, quest availability, whether guards shoot on sight, and it must be recoverable through disguises taken from faction armour. Build a main quest whose four mutually exclusive resolutions stay open until very late, so the player can work for several powers and commit at the end, with a long epilogue narrating the fate of every settlement and faction separately. Add skill checks shown INLINE in dialogue with the exact required value visible, so the player can see what a different build would have said. prompts.watchFor: A single reputation slider per faction instead of separate fame and infamy; reputation that does not change prices, greetings or hostility; faction disguises absent; a main quest that locks into one path early; a single ending or an epilogue that ignores side content; hidden skill checks with no visible requirement; hardcore mode as a damage multiplier rather than a resource-and-weight change; ammunition types with identical effect.

prompts.title: Mass Effect 2
prompts.prompt: Build Mass Effect 2 as a multi-file web third-person action role-playing game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), structured as a recruitment story: the player assembles a crew for a mission they are told nobody survives. The entire game must be built to serve its finale, which is the acceptance test — the SUICIDE MISSION is not a scripted ending but a computed one. Track, across the whole game, which squadmates have had their LOYALTY MISSION completed, which ship upgrades were purchased, and how long the player delayed after a specific trigger. Then run the finale as a sequence of assignments where the player picks a squadmate for each specialist ROLE — the tech specialist to seal a vent, the biotic to hold a barrier, a fire-team leader, an escort for the crew — and resolve each one against whether that character was loyal and suited to that job. Any squadmate can die permanently and so can the player, with the outcome being a direct function of preparation and assignment rather than difficulty. Around that, build cover-based squad combat with health, shields, armour and barriers each countered by different powers, a dialogue wheel with paragon and renegade options plus timed interrupts that let the player cut into a scene mid-sentence, and imported choices from a previous playthrough that change who is alive.
prompts.watchFor: A scripted finale where deaths are authored rather than computed from loyalty, upgrades and role assignment; squadmates who cannot permanently die, or deaths chosen randomly; loyalty missions that only grant a power; role assignments that have no consequence; a dialogue wheel with no timed interrupts; enemy defences that are all just health bars with no shield, armour and barrier counters; no imported prior-game state.

prompts.title: Civilization V
prompts.prompt: Build Civilization V as a multi-file web turn-based strategy game on a HEX grid, and build it around the rule that redefined the series' warfare: ONE UNIT PER TILE. No stacking is permitted, which means an army is a formation spread across terrain rather than a doomstack on a single square, and the acceptance test is that combat becomes a genuine tactical puzzle — melee units form a line to screen, RANGED units strike from one or two tiles behind that line without being counter-attacked, and the attacker must worry about being flanked and about having room to manoeuvre at all. Terrain, rivers, forests and hills must impose real movement and defence consequences on that positioning. Replace civics with SOCIAL POLICIES bought with accumulated CULTURE, arranged in mutually reinforcing branches that the player commits to progressively, so culture becomes a spendable strategic resource rather than only a border mechanic. Add CITY-STATES as a third kind of actor — minor powers that cannot win but can be courted with gold, gifts and quests to become allies supplying resources, units and votes, and that rival civilisations compete for. Keep strategic and luxury resources as hard build requirements and happiness inputs, add great people, a world congress of diplomacy, and several victory paths including culture, science, domination and diplomacy.
prompts.watchFor: A square grid, or hexes with unit stacking still allowed, which erases the entire tactical redesign; ranged units that suffer counter-attacks or that must be adjacent; terrain with no movement or defence effect; social policies as a simple government dropdown; culture that only expands borders; city-states as ordinary civilisations or as passive bonus tiles; a single victory condition.

prompts.title: Amnesia: The Dark Descent
prompts.prompt: Build Amnesia: The Dark Descent as a multi-file web first-person horror game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons). The first rule is absolute: THE PLAYER HAS NO WEAPONS AND CANNOT FIGHT. There is no combat system at all, so meeting a monster means running, hiding in a wardrobe or behind furniture, closing and barricading a door, or breaking line of sight — and the player must be unable even to attempt violence. The second rule is the SANITY system, which creates the game's central dilemma: standing in darkness drains sanity, and so does looking directly at a monster, and as it falls the screen distorts, the audio warps, footsteps stagger and the character eventually makes noise that ATTRACTS attention. Sanity is restored by standing in light and by progressing. Set against this a lantern that burns a finite oil supply and tinderboxes that light fixed candles and torches — a strictly limited stock — so light preserves sanity but consumes irreplaceable resources and makes the player visible. That trade is the acceptance test and must never be softened by regenerating oil or a free torch. Build interaction physically: doors are opened by grabbing the handle and dragging with the mouse at the speed the player chooses, drawers pull out, and objects are stacked and thrown, so opening a door slowly and quietly is a real choice.
prompts.watchFor: Any weapon or way to kill a monster; a sanity meter that has no perceptual or behavioural effect; darkness that costs nothing; unlimited lantern oil or tinderboxes; light that does not make the player more visible; doors that open on a key press instead of being physically dragged; monsters on fixed patrol loops that can be memorised; jump scares substituted for sustained pressure.

prompts.title: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim
prompts.prompt: Build The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim as a multi-file web open-world role-playing game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), in a cold northern province. Keep skills that improve BY USE, and attach to each one a PERK CONSTELLATION — a star-map of nodes with prerequisites and skill-level gates that the player spends one point in per level, so growth is use-driven at the base and choice-driven on top. Build DRAGON SHOUTS as the signature power: words of power are learned by finding word walls in the world, but a learned word is inert until the player absorbs a DRAGON SOUL to unlock it, and shouts are three words long with each word extending the effect, sharing a cooldown. Give the player a hand-per-input scheme where any combination of weapon, shield and spell can be held in the left and right hands independently, including dual-casting the same spell for an amplified version. Build a RADIANT QUEST system that generates ongoing work by filling templates with locations the player has not yet visited, NPCs who are still alive and items they do not have, so the world keeps producing content after the authored quests run out. Add a civil war with two joinable sides, guild questlines, smithing, enchanting and alchemy as crafting loops, and organise game content as data so it can be extended.
prompts.watchFor: Skills that level from experience points rather than from use; perks as a flat list with no prerequisites or skill gates; shouts purchasable or unlocked without both a word wall and a dragon soul; single-word shouts with no escalation; hands that cannot hold independent equipment or dual-cast; radiant quests replaced by a fixed finite list; a civil war with only one joinable side; content hard-coded so it cannot be extended.

prompts.title: Portal 2
prompts.prompt: Build Portal 2 as a multi-file web first-person puzzle game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), keeping recursive portal rendering and momentum conservation, then adding the systems that expand the vocabulary. The GELS are the headline and must be simulated as FLOWING FLUID, not painted decals: gel is pumped from pipes, falls, splashes, runs down slopes and COATS the surfaces it lands on, and a coating can be washed off by water. Propulsion gel makes a coated floor accelerate the player to high speed, repulsion gel makes a coated surface bounce anything that lands on it with conserved energy, and conversion gel makes any coated surface PORTALABLE — which turns the level's material layout itself into something the player edits. Add hard-light BRIDGES that are solid, project in a straight line and can be shot THROUGH A PORTAL so they emerge somewhere else at a new angle, and excursion FUNNELS that carry the player and cubes along a beam and likewise can be routed through portals and reversed. Include laser emitters with redirection cubes. Then build a separate CO-OPERATIVE campaign for two players with FOUR portals live at once, a ping and gesture system for communicating without voice, and puzzles that are genuinely impossible alone because they need two bodies in two places.
prompts.watchFor: Gels applied as static painted regions rather than a fluid that flows, splashes and coats; conversion gel that does not actually make a surface portalable; bridges and funnels that cannot be projected through a portal, which removes their point; funnels that cannot be reversed; a co-op mode that is the single-player campaign with two players; co-op puzzles solvable by one player; portals rendered as flat textures.

prompts.title: The Witcher 2: Assassins of Kings
prompts.prompt: Build The Witcher 2: Assassins of Kings as a multi-file web role-playing game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), in a world of grubby dynastic politics where every faction has a defensible position and a body count. The structural commitment that defines this game, and the acceptance test for the build, is the ACT TWO SPLIT: a single choice at the end of the first act sends the player into one of TWO ENTIRELY DIFFERENT SECOND ACTS — different location, different cast, different quests, different antagonist, different information about the plot — so a player finishing the game has seen roughly half of it, and the other half is only reachable by replaying from that decision. This must be two authored branches, not one branch with reskinned dialogue. Keep the series' preparation combat: potions and blade oils applied only before an encounter during meditation, bombs and traps laid in advance, signs used tactically rather than as damage, and rolls and parries that cost stamina, with a bestiary the player reads to learn what works. Add a dice poker and arm-wrestling diversion, a crafting system requiring diagrams and specific components, and choices whose consequences are deliberately unclear at the time and only resolve much later.
prompts.watchFor: A single middle act with different dialogue rather than two authored branches; the branch point signposted with a clearly better option; potions drinkable mid-combat; oils and bombs absent; signs used as ordinary attack spells; combat with unlimited rolling and no stamina; a bestiary that fills itself in; consequences that resolve immediately in the same scene.

prompts.title: Terraria
prompts.prompt: Build Terraria as a multi-file web 2D sandbox adventure with a procedurally generated world of tile columns running from a sky layer down through the surface, caverns and an underworld, split into biomes — forest, desert, corruption, jungle, snow, ocean — each with its own tiles, enemies and loot. Mining and building are tile-perfect and everything is placeable, with backgrounds walls distinct from solid tiles. Crafting runs off STATIONS: a recipe is only available when the player is standing near the workbench, anvil, furnace, or hellforge it requires, so progression is a chain of unlocking stations. The system that separates this from other sandboxes, and the acceptance test for the build, is that BOSSES REWRITE THE WORLD. Defeating a boss must not merely drop loot — it must mutate world generation and rules: beating the game's midpoint boss triggers hardmode, which carves new biome stripes diagonally across the existing map, spreads corruption and hallow through tiles over time, and causes ORES THAT DID NOT PREVIOUSLY EXIST to generate inside already-explored stone, so the player returns to old caves and finds new material. Add NPCs who move into houses the player builds once the house meets a checked set of requirements, each selling different goods, plus summoning items, accessories with stacking effects, and a full day/night and blood-moon event cycle.
prompts.watchFor: A static world where bosses only drop items; hardmode as a difficulty multiplier with no new ore generation or biome spread; crafting from a global menu with no station requirement; NPCs that arrive on a script rather than on validated player-built housing; a finite flat map with no biome variety or underworld; tiles that cannot be both mined and placed; no events or day/night cycle.

prompts.title: Deus Ex: Human Revolution
prompts.prompt: Build Deus Ex: Human Revolution as a multi-file web immersive sim using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), in a gold-tinted near-future about augmented humanity. Design every level explicitly around FOUR PILLARS — combat, stealth, hacking and social — and hold to the rule that each is a complete route: any objective must be reachable by fighting through, by never being seen, by hacking doors, turrets and cameras into compliance, or by talking to the right person, with vents, ducts, rooftops and side entrances built to serve them. Spend PRAXIS points on an augmentation tree covering cloak, heavy lifting, fall damage nullification, hacking capture and stealth software, punch-through-wall, and an energy cell system where only one cell recharges so powerful augs cost consumables. Build hacking as a real timed minigame: a node graph the player captures outward from an entry point, each capture rolling a detection chance that starts a countdown, with stealth and fortify software as spendable counters. The acceptance test is the SOCIAL BOSS FIGHT: certain confrontations are conversations played as encounters — the player reads the opponent's personality type, optionally uses a pheromone augmentation to sharpen the read, and chooses lines that push, appeal or ignore, and LOSING IS POSSIBLE and changes the outcome rather than reloading.
prompts.watchFor: Levels with one real route dressed as choice; hacking as an instant success on a skill check; conversations with no failure state, or with a single correct answer; the pheromone augmentation having no dialogue effect; augmentations as flat unlocks with no energy-cell economy; takedowns that are free; boss encounters that can only be resolved by shooting.

prompts.title: Counter-Strike: Global Offensive
prompts.prompt: Build Counter-Strike: Global Offensive as a multi-file web tactical shooter using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), keeping round-based play with no respawning, a carried-over buy economy, movement-dependent accuracy and deterministic learnable spray patterns. What this entry adds, and what the build must treat as a first-class system, is UTILITY AS SPATIAL CONTROL. Smoke grenades must produce a genuine VOLUMETRIC cloud that occludes vision in both directions, expands over time from where it lands, persists for a fixed duration and can be extinguished by an incendiary — so smokes are used to cut a map into pieces rather than to escape. Molotovs and incendiaries must lay a spreading fire on the ground that denies an area and damages anyone standing in it, forcing players out of positions without a shot. Flashbangs must blind based on where the player was actually LOOKING and whether the detonation was in line of sight, so a pop-flash thrown around a corner is a skill. Build a competitive format of fixed-length halves with a side switch, a loss-bonus that escalates over consecutive losses so a broken team can rebuild, and a skill-based matchmaking rank. Keep bomb plant and defuse with kit timings, and per-weapon economics where a losing round's rifle is a real investment.
prompts.watchFor: Smoke as a flat sprite or a one-way vision block rather than a volumetric two-way occluder; smoke that cannot be burnt away; incendiaries that damage but do not deny ground; flashbangs that blind regardless of view direction or line of sight; no side switch at half time; a flat loss bonus that does not escalate; random bullet cones instead of learnable spray patterns; respawning within a round.

prompts.title: Dishonored
prompts.prompt: Build Dishonored as a multi-file web immersive sim using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), in a whale-oil industrial city gripped by plague. The traversal verb is BLINK — a short-range instant teleport to a targeted point that the player aims and releases, silent and cheap — and the levels must be built as vertical playgrounds that assume it, with ledges, rooftops, window frames and beams that only make sense to someone who can jump the gap. Combine it with other powers on a mana economy: possession of a rat or a person to walk through a grate or past a checkpoint, time-stop, dark vision through walls, wind blast, and summoning rats. Every power must be combinable with the others in ways not explicitly designed. The system that gives the game its spine is CHAOS: the game counts how many people the player kills, and high chaos changes the WORLD ITSELF for the remaining missions — more rats, more plague victims in the streets, more guards on patrol, bleaker dialogue between characters, different late-mission events and a different ending — so lethality is a running commitment rather than an end-screen tally. Give every assassination target a non-lethal ELIMINATION that requires exploring an optional side path and that is usually a crueller fate than death.
prompts.watchFor: Chaos as a hidden score that only changes the final cutscene, rather than altering later missions' population, events and dialogue; blink as a dash with no verticality built around it; powers that cannot be combined; non-lethal target eliminations missing or reduced to knocking them out; levels with one route; a mana pool that fully regenerates so powers have no economy; guards with no investigation states.

prompts.title: XCOM: Enemy Unknown
prompts.prompt: Build XCOM: Enemy Unknown as a multi-file web turn-based tactics game with a strategic layer above it, modernising the original's design rather than copying it. On the tactical layer, each soldier gets TWO ACTIONS per turn — move then act, or dash twice — and the entire combat mathematics rests on COVER: tiles are annotated as full or half cover against specific directions, cover grants a large defence bonus shown honestly as a hit percentage on the targeting UI, and FLANKING — attacking from an angle where the target's cover does not apply — removes that bonus entirely and enables critical hits. This makes every turn a question of angles rather than damage, and it is the acceptance test. Add OVERWATCH to spend a turn covering an area and fire during the enemy's move, destructible cover so positions erode, and a fog of war where moving into an unseen pod ACTIVATES it and grants the aliens a free reposition. Soldiers are randomly generated, nameable, gain a CLASS on promotion and then choose one of two perks at each subsequent rank, and they die PERMANENTLY. On the strategic layer, build the base as a cutaway view, launch interceptors, research and manufacture from recovered alien materials, and manage panic per funding nation where too much panic loses them.
prompts.watchFor: Cover as a flat damage reduction with no directionality or flanking rule; hit chances hidden from the player; no overwatch; indestructible cover; enemy pods that are always active rather than activating on sight; soldiers who are interchangeable or who respawn after death; classes with a fixed perk path instead of a choice at each rank; a strategic layer that is only a mission select with no research, panic or funding.

prompts.title: FTL: Faster Than Light
prompts.prompt: Build FTL: Faster Than Light as a multi-file web spaceship roguelike where the player commands the SHIP rather than piloting it, viewed as a cutaway of rooms. The central mechanic is the REACTOR: a finite number of power bars must be allocated in real time between shields, engines, weapons, oxygen, medbay, doors and sensors, and there is never enough, so every fight is a live argument about what to switch off — cutting oxygen to fire one more volley, dropping shields to outrun a missile. That allocation is the acceptance test. Combat is real-time WITH PAUSE against another ship shown as its own cutaway, and the player targets specific ENEMY SUBSYSTEMS rather than a health bar: knock out their weapons, breach their oxygen, disable their piloting to stop them fleeing, or vent their crew. Crew members are individuals who must physically WALK to a station to boost it, fight boarders hand to hand, repair damaged systems and put out fires, gaining skill at what they do and dying permanently. Fire spreads room to room and consumes oxygen, and hull breaches vent it, so doors become a weapon the player uses on their own ship. Build a branching sector map where an advancing enemy fleet forces constant forward movement, random events with text choices, and permadeath with unlockable starting ships.
prompts.watchFor: Direct control of the ship's flight instead of system management; power as an abstract resource rather than a finite bar count reallocated live; combat against a single enemy health bar with no targetable subsystems; crew as passive stat bonuses who do not walk, repair or fight; fire and breaches with no spread or oxygen consumption; a linear map with no pursuing fleet pressure; runs that persist on death.

prompts.title: Hotline Miami
prompts.prompt: Build Hotline Miami as a multi-file web top-down action game drenched in neon and driven by a synth soundtrack. The rule that makes it work is symmetrical lethality: EVERYONE DIES IN ONE HIT, including the player, so a floor of a building is not a combat encounter but a PUZZLE attempted at speed, where the player learns the layout and the patrol routes by dying repeatedly. That requires the second essential property — RESTART MUST BE INSTANT, on a single key, with no loading, no death animation to sit through and no menu, so the loop between failure and the next attempt is under a second and dying twenty times in a row stays fluid rather than punishing. Build enemies who react to what they perceive: they hear gunshots from other rooms and come to investigate, they see bodies, they see through doorways down long sight lines, and dogs behave differently from armed guards. Give the player a melee and firearm arsenal where guns are loud and summon the floor while bats and knives are silent, doors can be slammed into enemies to stun them, and downed enemies must be executed as a separate action. Build the ANIMAL MASKS as rule modifiers chosen before a level — one starts the player with a weapon, one makes dogs ignore them, one makes door-slams lethal, one changes the score — and score chains for speed, variety and boldness.
prompts.watchFor: A health bar on the player or on enemies, which removes the puzzle framing entirely; a death screen, load pause or menu between attempts; enemies who do not hear gunfire or investigate; no line-of-sight through doorways; masks as cosmetic skins with no rule changes; executions handled automatically; a score that does not reward chaining, speed or weapon variety.

prompts.title: Dota 2
prompts.prompt: Build a playable web slice of Dota 2 as a multi-file game — three lanes, a jungle, two bases and a modest hero roster — preserving the mechanics that make it the harsher, deeper lane game. Gold comes from LAST-HITTING enemy creeps, but the defining addition is DENYING: a player may attack and kill their OWN creeps once they fall below a health threshold, which denies the opponent both the gold and a share of the experience, so laning is a two-sided contest over every single creep and the acceptance test is that denying is implemented and actually withholds experience. Build a real item ECONOMY where the shop sells components that combine into recipes, many items have ACTIVE abilities as important as a hero's own spells, and a COURIER unit must physically ferry purchases from the base shop to the hero in lane, where it can be intercepted and killed. Make death expensive — a gold penalty and a respawn timer that scales steeply with level — so a single mistake has a long tail. Add high-ground miss chance for attackers shooting uphill, a day and night cycle that changes vision ranges and unit behaviour, a powerful neutral boss whose kill grants a reusable resurrection item, hero turn rates and animation commitment that make repositioning a real cost, and fog of war lifted by placed observer wards.
prompts.watchFor: No deny mechanic, which removes the defining laning skill; denies that withhold gold but not experience; items as flat stat purchases with no active abilities or component recipes; no courier, so shopping is instant and riskless; a flat respawn timer with no gold loss; no high-ground miss chance; heroes that turn and act instantly with no animation commitment; no wards or fog of war.

prompts.title: BioShock Infinite
prompts.prompt: Build BioShock Infinite as a multi-file web first-person shooter using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), set in a bright, unsettling city floating in the clouds. Two systems carry it. The SKY-LINE is traversal and combat at once: rails are threaded through the open air between buildings, and the player hooks on with a wrist device, rides at speed, can reverse direction mid-ride, can slow and hold position, may fire while riding, and can DISMOUNT INTO A DROP ATTACK on an enemy below — so an arena is a three-dimensional circuit rather than a floor with cover, and encounters must be designed as such. The second is the COMPANION, and she must never be a burden: she cannot be killed or lost, she needs no protection, and instead she actively helps — spotting and THROWING the player ammunition, health and salts mid-fight at the moment they run dry. Her defining ability is the TEAR: rifts to other realities that she can be asked to open at marked points during combat, pulling in a piece of another world — cover, a turret, an ally, a supply crate, a hook point — but only ONE at a time, so the player is constantly choosing which reality to have open. Add vigors in the left hand and firearms in the right, with a two-weapon limit and regenerating shields over a health pool.
prompts.watchFor: Sky-lines as scripted rail rides between arenas rather than a usable combat surface; no reversing, holding or drop attack; a companion who must be escorted or protected, or who can die; the companion supplying nothing during fights; tears as a scripted cutscene instead of a player-requested combat option; multiple tears open at once, removing the choice; vigors as reskinned grenades with no environmental interaction.

prompts.title: Path of Exile
prompts.prompt: Build Path of Exile as a multi-file web isometric action RPG built for build-crafting depth rather than for a smooth first hour. Three systems define it. First, ONE ENORMOUS SHARED PASSIVE TREE: a single sprawling web of hundreds of small nodes — stat increments, keystones that change a rule outright, notable clusters — where the classes are not separate trees but merely different STARTING POINTS on the same map, so a character build is a ROUTE travelled across that web and two classes can converge on the same region. Second, SKILLS AS ITEMS: active abilities are gems socketed into sockets on equipment, and SUPPORT gems placed in sockets LINKED to them modify their behaviour — added projectiles, chaining, area increase, faster casting — so the player's core ability is assembled from the gear they wear, and finding a piece with more linked sockets is a bigger upgrade than more damage. Third, an economy with NO GOLD: currency is a set of crafting orbs that each have a real use on items, so every purchase is paid for by giving up a crafting action, and trading is barter between players. Add randomised map layouts, item affix rolling gated by item level, and an endgame of modifiable maps that the player rolls with dangerous properties for better rewards.
prompts.watchFor: Separate per-class skill trees instead of one shared web with different entry points; keystones that are only stat bonuses rather than rule changes; skills learned from a class list instead of socketed gems; support gems that do not require linked sockets; a gold currency, which removes the crafting-versus-buying tension; fixed hand-authored maps; affixes not gated by item level; an endgame that is only higher difficulty.

prompts.title: The Stanley Parable
prompts.prompt: Build The Stanley Parable as a multi-file web first-person narrative game about the illusion of choice in games. An omniscient NARRATOR describes the protagonist's actions in the past tense, frequently BEFORE the player performs them — 'Stanley entered the door on his left' — and the entire game is the space between what the narrator says and what the player does. The design law, and the acceptance test, is that DISOBEDIENCE MUST ALWAYS LEAD TO AUTHORED CONTENT: whenever the player takes the other door, refuses to move, walks backwards, or breaks the intended sequence, they must be met with fresh narration written for exactly that act and with new rooms, not with an invisible wall, a generic line or a fail state. Build the office building as a space that RECONFIGURES around choices, opening areas that were not there before and closing ones that were, sometimes visibly contradicting itself. Write many distinct ENDINGS reached through different patterns of compliance and defiance, each of which terminates the story and RESTARTS the game at the beginning, with the narrator carrying knowledge of what happened last time into the new run so repetition itself becomes the medium. Include escalating sequences where the narrator attempts to regain control, negotiates, sulks, and rebuilds the level around the player.
prompts.watchFor: Invisible walls or scripted nudges that force the player back to the intended path; a generic catch-all line for unhandled disobedience instead of authored content; a single ending, or endings that just show a screen without restarting the loop; a narrator who does not remember previous runs; a static level that never reconfigures; combat, puzzles or fail states, none of which belong here.

prompts.title: Papers, Please
prompts.prompt: Build Papers, Please as a multi-file web game about being an immigration inspector at a border checkpoint in a grey authoritarian state. The core loop is FINDING CONTRADICTIONS between documents: an applicant hands over a passport, an entry permit, a work pass, an ID card, and the player must cross-check names, dates, issuing cities, photographs, weights, seals and expiry against each other AND against a RULEBOOK that gains a new page nearly every day — one day only citizens, the next day foreigners with entry tickets, then a required vaccination certificate, then a specific city excluded — so the same job gets steadily harder as the rules accrete. Build the desk as a physically CRAMPED workspace where documents are dragged around, overlapped, hidden under each other and must be shuffled to compare two at once, because the friction of the desk is the difficulty. When the player spots a discrepancy they must highlight the two conflicting fields to interrogate the applicant. Pay is per correctly processed person, docked for mistakes, and each night it is spent against rent, heat, food and medicine for a family who get COLD, SICK AND DIE if underfunded. Layer moral pressure over the arithmetic: people whose papers are wrong but whose reasons are true, bribes, and a resistance asking for small acts of sabotage.
prompts.watchFor: An automatic validity check or a highlight that points out discrepancies for the player; a rulebook that does not grow day by day; documents laid out in a tidy grid with no overlap or dragging, which removes the desk friction; pay disconnected from the family's survival, or family members who cannot actually die; every applicant being either clearly valid or clearly fake, with no cases where the rules and the right thing to do conflict.

prompts.title: Divinity: Original Sin
prompts.prompt: Build Divinity: Original Sin as a multi-file web isometric turn-based role-playing game. The combat model is an ELEMENTAL SURFACE SIMULATION and it is the whole appeal: spells and objects deposit persistent SURFACES and CLOUDS onto the battlefield grid that spread, linger and — crucially — COMBINE according to consistent physical rules rather than scripted pairs. Rain creates water; a lightning spell into water electrifies the whole connected pool and stuns everyone standing in it; fire on water becomes steam that blocks line of sight; fire on oil creates a spreading blaze; poison clouds IGNITE explosively when hit by fire; ice makes a surface slippery so units fall over; and blood from wounds is itself a conductive surface. The acceptance test is that these interactions must fall out of a general surface system, so combinations the designers never listed still work. Build turn-based combat on action points with movement, attacks and abilities all drawing from the same pool, and initiative that interleaves both sides. Make CO-OP first-class: two players each control characters, both may act in dialogue, and when they disagree the game resolves it with a contest between the players rather than by deferring to a host. Add an interactive world where nearly everything can be picked up, moved, stolen, teleported or crafted.
prompts.watchFor: Elemental effects as damage types with no persistent surfaces on the ground; surfaces that do not spread or that only combine in a hardcoded list of pairs; poison clouds that do not ignite, or water that does not conduct; a shared action pool split into separate move and attack allowances; co-op where only the host makes dialogue choices; no disagreement resolution between players; a world where scenery cannot be moved or stolen.

prompts.title: Alien: Isolation
prompts.prompt: Build Alien: Isolation as a multi-file web survival horror game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), aboard a decaying space station in a used, analogue, seventies-futurist style. There is ONE creature, it is UNKILLABLE, and its behaviour must be genuinely unscripted — this is the entire game and the acceptance test. Build its intelligence in two tiers that do not share knowledge. An unseen DIRECTOR always knows roughly where the player is and steers the creature toward that region, controlling pacing by pulling it away when tension has been sustained too long. The CREATURE ITSELF does not know where the player is and must find them with its own senses: hearing footsteps at a volume scaled by movement speed and surface, hearing doors and lockers, seeing down corridors and through glass, investigating noises, searching rooms, checking under desks and inside lockers, and — critically — hearing the player's own MOTION TRACKER when it is held up, so the tool that tells you where it is also tells it where you are. It must never spawn on a trigger, never follow a patrol route, and must LEARN over a session, becoming less fooled by a hiding place used repeatedly. Give the player only deterrents — a flamethrower that drives it off temporarily, noisemakers, flares — plus crafted items, hostile humans and androids, and manual SAVE STATIONS that take real time and do not pause the world.
prompts.watchFor: A scripted alien on patrol routes or spawn triggers, which makes it memorisable and destroys the tension; a creature that shares the director's knowledge of the player's exact position; the alien being killable; a motion tracker that carries no risk of being heard; hiding places that always work no matter how often they are used; checkpoint autosaves instead of timed manual save stations; the alien absent for long stretches of the middle game.

prompts.title: Dark Souls II
prompts.prompt: Build Dark Souls II as a multi-file web action role-playing game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons). Combat is deliberate and COMMITTED: every swing, roll, block and sprint spends STAMINA from a bar that regenerates only when idle and is reduced by blocking, and every animation has wind-up and a recovery period during which the player cannot cancel or act, so an attack is a decision the player must live through. Locking on, spacing, and reading an enemy's wind-up are the skills. SOULS are simultaneously experience and currency spent on levels, equipment and repairs, and on death the entire held amount is DROPPED at the place of death, recoverable exactly once — die again on the way back and it is gone forever. Bonfires are the only checkpoints and resting at one restores flasks while RESPAWNING every ordinary enemy in the world. Build this entry's own additions honestly: each death permanently lowers maximum health in steps toward roughly half, reversible only by consuming a scarce item, so a bad run compounds; ordinary enemies stop respawning after being killed about a dozen times, letting a stuck player grind an area empty; and invincibility frames on the roll are governed by a levelable stat rather than being fixed. Add interconnected level design, item-described lore, and asynchronous multiplayer through messages, bloodstains, invasions and summons.
prompts.watchFor: Attacks that can be cancelled or that cost no stamina; rolling with unlimited spam; souls that are not lost on death, or that can be recovered repeatedly; bonfires that do not respawn enemies; the escalating health loss on death omitted; enemies that respawn forever with no depletion; roll invincibility fixed rather than stat-driven; explicit lore delivered by cutscene instead of item descriptions; no asynchronous multiplayer traces.

prompts.title: Dragon Age: Inquisition
prompts.prompt: Build Dragon Age: Inquisition as a multi-file web party role-playing game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), where the player leads an organisation rather than a party. Keep real-time-with-pause combat over a party of four with a pull-back TACTICAL CAMERA that can be held indefinitely while orders are queued, and companions with approval, banter and personal arcs. The system that structures the whole game is the WAR TABLE: a strategic map of the world where the Inquisition spends accumulated POWER and INFLUENCE to unlock new regions and advance the plot, and where operations are dispatched to one of three advisors — military force, subterfuge, or diplomacy — with each advisor offering a DIFFERENT resolution to the same problem at a different real-time cost and a different reward and narrative consequence. Operations then run on a clock while the player goes off and plays, resolving later. Build several large open zones each with their own faction, environmental hazards, camps to establish that extend the party's reach, and rifts that must be closed by fighting waves and then sealing the tear. Add crafting where the materials chosen determine the resulting item's statistics, judgement scenes where the player sentences captured enemies, and Inquisition perks bought with influence.
prompts.watchFor: A war table that is only a quest menu with no advisor choice, no real-time operation clocks and no differing outcomes; regions unlocked by story progress rather than spent power; a tactical camera that cannot be freely positioned or that unpauses itself; open zones filled with markers but no faction, hazards or camps; crafting with fixed recipes where material choice does not change the result; judgements with no consequence; companions with approval that gates nothing.

prompts.title: Shovel Knight
prompts.prompt: Build Shovel Knight as a multi-file web 2D action platformer that honours eight-bit constraints as a design discipline rather than as a filter: a restricted palette with a limited number of colours per sprite, chunky pixel art on a low internal resolution, deliberate sprite flicker on crowded lines, and a chiptune score — while quietly allowing modern conveniences the original hardware could not manage. The universal verb is the DOWNWARD THRUST, a pogo attack performed by holding down and jumping, and it must serve three purposes at once, which is the acceptance test: it is an attack, it is a BOUNCE that gains height off enemies, off projectiles, off hazards and off bouncable scenery, and it is therefore a traversal tool, so whole sequences are crossed by pogoing across a chain of objects without touching the ground. Build a world map with branching paths, wandering encounters and multiple routes to bosses. Make CHECKPOINTS a risk-reward decision: each one can be deliberately DESTROYED by the player for a burst of treasure, permanently removing it from the level. Add relics bought with gold that grant secondary abilities, armour and shovel upgrades that change movement and damage, health and magic upgrades hidden in the levels, and knight bosses with learnable, telegraphed attack patterns and a second phase.
prompts.watchFor: Modern high-resolution art or unrestricted colour, which abandons the discipline; a downward thrust that damages but cannot bounce off enemies, projectiles or scenery; levels that never require pogo traversal; checkpoints that cannot be destroyed for treasure; a linear stage select with no world map or branching; bosses with random attacks instead of learnable telegraphed patterns; upgrades that are pure stat increases with no effect on movement.

prompts.title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
prompts.prompt: Build The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt as a multi-file web open-world role-playing game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons). The reputation to earn here is QUEST WRITING, so the structure must serve it: side quests are not fetch tasks with a marker but authored short stories that begin as something mundane, turn out to be something else, and end without a clean moral resolution — and the acceptance test is that a randomly chosen side quest should contain a reversal and at least two endings neither of which is obviously correct. Build the monster CONTRACT loop as investigation rather than combat: the contract is taken from a noticeboard, the client is interviewed for details that may be wrong, the site is examined in a heightened SENSES mode that highlights tracks, blood and scents which are then FOLLOWED to reconstruct what happened, the bestiary entry is read to learn the creature's weakness, and only then does the player prepare the correct oil, sign, bomb and potion during meditation before fighting. Preparation must be mandatory rather than optional. Add a large continuous world with distinct regions, mounted travel and sailing, a full collectible CARD GAME playable against most NPCs with its own deck-building, and choices whose consequences surface many hours later in places the player has left behind.
prompts.watchFor: Side quests as marker-following fetch tasks with one outcome; contracts that skip investigation and go straight to a fight; senses mode that simply points at the objective instead of revealing a followable trail; the bestiary auto-filled so reading is never needed; oils, signs and potions optional because raw damage always works; consequences that resolve in the same scene; the card game reduced to a scripted minigame with no deck-building.

prompts.title: Grand Theft Auto V (PC Release)
prompts.prompt: Build Grand Theft Auto V as a multi-file web open-world crime game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), across a large simulated city and its surrounding countryside. Two structural systems define this entry. First, THREE PROTAGONISTS the player switches between at almost any moment: the camera pulls up and out into the sky and drops back down onto whichever of the three is chosen, and critically the other two have been LIVING while away — the player arrives mid-activity, finding one waking on a beach, one mid-argument, one being chased — so the world continues without them. Each has a unique special ability on a meter. Second, HEISTS as multi-stage operations rather than missions: the player is presented with a CHOICE OF APPROACH (loud and fast, or quiet and slow), then HIRES a crew of gunmen, drivers and hackers from a roster where each has a skill rating and demands a percentage CUT, so a cheap crew leaves more money but is likelier to fail and get killed; then runs preparation missions to gather the specific vehicles and equipment that approach requires; then executes the job, switching between protagonists mid-heist as their roles interleave. Add a wanted level with escalating police response and line-of-sight escape, and structure the code so content is data-driven and moddable.
prompts.watchFor: A single protagonist, or switching that teleports to a static idle character with no ongoing life; special abilities that are identical across the three; heists as linear missions with no approach choice, no crew hiring and no cut negotiation; crew skill that has no effect on the outcome; preparation missions absent; a wanted level that ends on a timer rather than on breaking line of sight; a city that is a track rather than a simulation.

prompts.title: Undertale
prompts.prompt: Build Undertale as a multi-file web role-playing game whose central claim is that you never have to kill anyone. Every single encounter, including bosses, must have a MERCY route: each monster has its own specific sequence of ACT options — flirt, joke, hum, compliment, threaten, or something particular to that creature — which, performed correctly, makes it spareable, and the correct sequence must be discoverable from what the monster says and does. Killing is always possible and always easier, and that asymmetry is the point.
