Invert the combat interface so the ENEMY'S TURN is the interactive part: the player controls a small heart inside a bounded box and must dodge a bullet-hell pattern authored specifically for that character's personality, with the box itself changing shape and the heart's physics changing (gravity, colour-locked movement) for particular fights. The other requirement is PERSISTENCE ACROSS RESETS: the game writes state outside the ordinary save, so deleting a save, resetting or replaying is itself noticed, characters remember previous runs, and a route completed once cannot simply be undone. Make a full pacifist run and a full genocide run produce substantially different games — different scenes, different bosses, different endings — rather than a different final line.
prompts.watchFor: Encounters that can only be resolved by combat, or a generic 'spare' button with no per-monster ACT sequence; the enemy turn as a damage number instead of a dodging minigame; bullet patterns reused across characters; no persistence outside the save file, so resets are invisible; pacifist and genocide routes differing only in the ending screen; the correct ACT sequence given to the player rather than deduced.

prompts.title: Rocket League
prompts.prompt: Build Rocket League as a multi-file web game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons) and a real rigid-body physics engine: rocket-powered cars playing football in an enclosed arena with a giant ball. There are no abilities, no power-ups and no stats — ALL of the depth must come out of the vehicle physics, so those have to be exactly right. Build a car with suspension, grip that breaks into a drift, and a BOOST resource collected from pads on the floor. Give it a jump, and then a second input within a window that becomes either a straight double jump or, if a direction is held, a DODGE FLIP — a rotational lunge that imparts real momentum to the car and to anything it strikes. Make surfaces MAGNETIC so a car driving up a wall or across the ceiling sticks and keeps its orientation, and make the transition on and off those surfaces smooth. Above all build AERIALS: once airborne the player controls pitch, yaw and roll freely and thrusts with boost, so flying is a full six-degree-of-freedom problem and hitting a moving ball in mid-air is the skill ceiling. Ball and car collisions must be predictable and consistent so players can learn to aim. Add a ball-cam toggle, demolitions at high speed, kickoffs, overtime, and online multiplayer with prediction.
prompts.watchFor: Scripted or assisted shots instead of pure physics collisions; flips that are an animation with no momentum transfer; no wall or ceiling driving, or transitions that eject the car; aerials with restricted or auto-levelled air control; boost as a cooldown rather than a collectable resource with pads; a ball with inconsistent restitution so aiming cannot be learned; abilities or power-ups, which do not belong.

prompts.title: Rainbow Six Siege
prompts.prompt: Build Rainbow Six Siege as a multi-file web tactical shooter using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons). DESTRUCTION is the tactical language and must be granular, not scripted: interior walls, floors and ceilings are soft surfaces that can be shot through, blown open with breaching charges, or carved into small MURDER HOLES with a few shotgun blasts, so the players — not the level designer — decide where the sightlines and the entrances are. A hole in a ceiling turns a room into a two-storey fight; a hatch blown in the floor opens a vertical attack. The round structure is one life each and two phases. In the PREPARATION phase the defenders barricade doors and windows, place traps and gadgets, and reinforce specific walls with a LIMITED number of unbreakable panels — so choosing which walls stay soft is the core defensive decision — while attackers pilot small drones through the building to find the objective and mark defenders. Then the assault begins with the attackers' drones still usable as cameras. Build asymmetric OPERATORS who each carry one unique gadget that hard-counters something else — a thermal charge that opens reinforced walls, a jammer that disables electronics, a shield, a camera, a trap — so team composition is a counter puzzle. Include destructible cameras, rappelling on exterior walls and leaning.
prompts.watchFor: Destruction limited to marked breach points, which removes player-authored sightlines; walls that are either indestructible or fully destructible with no reinforcement choice; no vertical destruction through floors and ceilings; no preparation phase, drones or gadget placement; operators who differ only in weapon loadout; respawning within a round; gadgets with no counters, so one operator dominates.

prompts.title: DOOM (2016)
prompts.prompt: Build DOOM (2016) as a multi-file web first-person shooter using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), designed explicitly against the conventions of modern shooters: no cover system, no regenerating health, no reloading, no sprint button that slows your weapon, and no scripted cinematic pauses. The engine of the whole design is PUSH-FORWARD COMBAT, built on two resource loops that must be the player's ONLY sustain. First, GLORY KILLS: an enemy that has taken enough damage enters a staggered state and flashes, and a melee finisher on a staggered enemy plays a quick brutal animation and DROPS HEALTH — so the only way to heal in a firefight is to run at the thing trying to kill you. Second, the CHAINSAW: fuelled by a scarce resource, cutting an enemy in half showers AMMUNITION — so running dry means charging in as well. Together these must make retreating and hiding strictly losing strategies, which is the acceptance test. Build arenas that seal on entry, with high mobility, double jumps, ledge grabs and vertical loops that keep the player circling. Give a full weapon wheel with two swappable MODS per gun that change its role, upgrade currencies, and a demon roster whose members each demand a different movement answer.
prompts.watchFor: Regenerating health or health pickups that make glory kills optional; a cover system or enemies that let the player camp a corner; reloading; glory kills as a damage animation with no health reward; a chainsaw that does not drop ammunition; arenas that can be cleared from a doorway; weapon mods that are stat boosts rather than role changes; slow movement or an aim-down-sights-centred design.

prompts.title: Overwatch
prompts.prompt: Build Overwatch as a multi-file web hero shooter using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), with a bright readable art style where every hero is identifiable by silhouette, colour and audio at a distance. Build a roster of radically different heroes across damage, tank and support roles — not classes with shared weapons, but individuals with unique movement, unique primary fire and two or three unique abilities on separate cooldowns, including some who fly, wall-run, teleport, deploy shields or reposition allies. The structural mechanic that separates this from its predecessors, and the acceptance test, is that heroes can be SWAPPED MID-MATCH: any player may return to spawn and change hero at any time, so a match is a live counter-picking argument in which a team losing to a sniper switches to something that closes distance, and a good composition is a moving target rather than a pre-match choice. Build ULTIMATE abilities charged by doing the job — damage dealt, healing done, objective time — that are announced by a loud, distinct SPOKEN VOICE LINE audible to BOTH teams, so an ultimate is telegraphed and can be answered, and ultimate management becomes a team-level economy. Ship objective modes only — payload escort, control point capture and hybrid — with no plain deathmatch, and add a hero-based lock preventing duplicates.
prompts.watchFor: Heroes locked in at match start, which removes the counter-picking layer entirely; heroes built from a shared weapon pool with an ability bolted on; ultimates charged on a timer rather than by contribution; ultimates that fire silently with no audible telegraph to either team; deathmatch as the primary mode; silhouettes and voice lines too similar to identify quickly; abilities sharing one cooldown.

prompts.title: Stardew Valley
prompts.prompt: Build Stardew Valley as a multi-file web farming and life simulation. The tension that makes it compelling is SCARCITY OF TIME, and it must be enforced strictly: each day runs on a clock from morning until the character collapses at a fixed late hour, and every action also costs ENERGY from a bar that only refills by sleeping or eating, so a day holds a limited number of actions and the player must constantly choose between watering the crops, going down the mine, fishing, foraging and visiting people. Layer a SEASONAL calendar over that — each crop grows only in its season and DIES when the season turns, so planting is a commitment against a deadline, and each season brings its own forage, fish and festivals. Build villagers as individuals with daily and seasonal schedules, distinct likes and dislikes for gifts with a limited number of gifts per week, heart levels that unlock cutscenes revealing they have real problems, and marriage. Add a procedurally generated mine descending in floors with combat, ore tiers and elevator checkpoints; a fishing minigame of keeping a bar over a struggling fish; crafting, artisan goods that multiply value; and multiple competing skill tracks so no single run can max everything.
prompts.watchFor: An unlimited day or no energy cost, which collapses every meaningful choice; crops that survive a season change; villagers with no schedules or with universal gift preferences; hearts that unlock nothing; a static mine with no procedural floors or depth progression; fishing as a single click; artisan processing with no time cost; a progression where all skills can be maxed in one run without trade-offs.

prompts.title: Dark Souls III
prompts.prompt: Build Dark Souls III as a multi-file web action role-playing game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), faster and more aggressive than its predecessors while keeping stamina-governed commitment, souls dropped on death and recoverable once, and bonfires that respawn every enemy. This entry's own systems must be present. FOCUS POINTS are a second blue resource alongside stamina, spent by both spellcasting AND by WEAPON ARTS — a unique special move built into each individual weapon, entered from a ready stance, so a greatsword's art differs from a curved sword's and choosing a weapon is choosing a moveset rather than a damage number. The flask allocation is the acceptance test: the player holds a fixed total number of Estus flasks and must DIVIDE them before setting out between health flasks and focus flasks, so a caster gives up healing and a melee character gives up their weapon arts, and the split can only be changed at a bonfire. Build enemies that punish the greedy: attacks with deliberately DELAYED wind-ups that bait a panic roll, multi-hit combos that continue after the first hit lands, and bosses with a second phase that changes moveset entirely. Add poise, interconnected level design, item-description lore and asynchronous multiplayer traces.
prompts.watchFor: Weapon arts absent or shared across all weapons; spells and arts drawing from separate resources instead of one focus pool; a fixed flask split the player cannot allocate; enemy attacks with uniform timing that never bait a roll; bosses whose second phase is only more health; stamina that regenerates during attacks; souls not lost on death; explicit narrative cutscenes instead of item-description lore.

prompts.title: Civilization VI
prompts.prompt: Build Civilization VI as a multi-file web turn-based strategy game on hexes, keeping one unit per tile, and built around the change that redefined city planning: DISTRICT UNSTACKING. A city is no longer a single tile with a build list — specialised districts are constructed onto SEPARATE tiles in the city's territory, each with its own buildings and its own placement rules: a campus, a holy site, a harbour that must be on coast, an industrial zone, a theatre square, a commercial hub, an encampment. Every district earns ADJACENCY BONUSES computed from what surrounds the tile it is placed on — a campus beside mountains and rainforest, a holy site beside natural wonders, an industrial zone beside mines, a harbour beside the city centre — so laying out a city becomes a spatial optimisation puzzle across real terrain, and that adjacency computation is the acceptance test. Run a second progression track in parallel with the tech tree: a CIVICS tree advanced by culture that unlocks governments, each of which provides a number of typed POLICY CARD slots that the player slots and re-slots freely between military, economic, diplomatic and wildcard cards, so strategy can be reconfigured turn to turn. Add eurekas and inspirations that discount a technology or civic when the player performs a related act, and city-states with envoys.
prompts.watchFor: Cities as a single tile with a flat build list, which discards the entire design; districts that are buildings with no map placement; adjacency bonuses absent or a fixed flat number regardless of surrounding terrain; a single tech tree with no parallel civics track; governments as one dropdown with no policy card slots; cards that cannot be swapped after being set; no eurekas, so research is unaffected by what the player actually does.

prompts.title: Divinity: Original Sin II
prompts.prompt: Build Divinity: Original Sin II as a multi-file web isometric turn-based role-playing game, keeping and deepening the elemental SURFACE simulation — spreading, combining fluids and clouds where water conducts electricity, fire turns water to sight-blocking steam, poison ignites, oil burns and blood conducts — and adding blessed and cursed variants of each surface that behave differently. The system this sequel is defined by, and the acceptance test, is DUAL ARMOUR: every character carries a PHYSICAL ARMOUR pool and a MAGIC ARMOUR pool over their health, and no crowd control of a given type can land until the corresponding pool is at ZERO — a stun cannot apply while magic armour remains, a knockdown cannot apply while physical armour remains — regardless of how many are attempted. This turns disabling an enemy into a two-stage commitment of focused fire rather than a lucky roll, and eliminates chain-stunning entirely. Build ORIGIN characters with their own histories, agendas and quests, each playable as the protagonist or recruited as a companion, whose personal goals can directly conflict with the party's. Add height advantage affecting accuracy and range, teleportation as a tactical tool for repositioning enemies into hazards, armour and weapon crafting, and four-player co-op where players may argue, split up, steal from each other and even fight.
prompts.watchFor: A single armour pool, or crowd control that lands on a percentage chance while armour remains, which reintroduces stun-locking; surfaces that do not spread or combine; no blessed or cursed variants; origin characters as ordinary recruitable companions with no agenda of their own; height with no combat effect; co-op restricted so only the host decides dialogue, or players who cannot act against each other.

prompts.title: Hollow Knight
prompts.prompt: Build Hollow Knight as a multi-file web 2D metroidvania through a vast, sombre, hand-drawn ruined kingdom of insects. Mapping is a mechanic rather than a service, and this is the acceptance test: the player does NOT receive a map. Each area's map must be BOUGHT from a wandering cartographer who has to be found somewhere in that area first, the purchased map only reveals what has been walked, and — critically — it only UPDATES when the player sits at a bench, so exploring deep into unknown territory means navigating from memory with a stale map. Seeing the player's own position on that map requires equipping a compass CHARM, which costs a notch. CHARMS are the build system: found throughout the world, each costs a number of notches from a slowly growing limited pool, and they change rules rather than adding numbers — faster healing, ranged attacks from soul, a companion, damage while at one health. SOUL is harvested by striking enemies and spent either on spells or on HEALING, which requires standing still and channelling, so healing is a risk taken in a gap in the pattern. On death, all currency drops with a SHADE at the place of death that must be fought to reclaim it. Build interconnected areas gated by traversal abilities, and long boss fights with learnable telegraphs.
prompts.watchFor: A map given automatically or one that updates in real time as the player walks, which removes the disorientation the game is built on; position shown without the compass charm; charms as flat stat boosts with unlimited slots; healing that is instant or usable while moving; soul used only for spells; death with no shade to recover; a linear area order with no traversal-gated backtracking.

prompts.title: PUBG: Battlegrounds
prompts.prompt: Build PUBG as a multi-file web battle royale using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons): a large island, many players, one life each, last one standing wins. The match must begin with the DROP as a real decision — a transport aircraft crosses the map along a randomly chosen straight flight path each match, players choose when to jump, then control their freefall and parachute to steer toward a landing spot, so the plane's path determines which towns will be contested and every match opens differently. Players start with NOTHING and everything is scavenged from world spawns: weapons, attachments, armour, helmets, backpacks that increase carrying capacity, medical items and fuel. The pacing engine, and the acceptance test, is the shrinking BLUE ZONE: a circular safe area whose next, smaller circle is chosen RANDOMLY somewhere inside the current one and telegraphed on the map before it closes, with everything outside taking escalating damage over time — so players are forced into ever-closer proximity on a schedule, the endgame is guaranteed, and a good position can become a death trap. Build ballistics with bullet drop, travel time and per-weapon velocity requiring aim above the target at range, attachments that modify recoil and handling, drivable vehicles, prone and lean, and loud directional audio where footsteps and gunfire are the primary information.
prompts.watchFor: A fixed spawn or a fixed plane path each match; players starting with a chosen loadout instead of scavenging; a safe zone that shrinks toward the map centre every time, which makes position predictable; a zone that kills instantly rather than damaging over time; hitscan weapons with no drop or travel time; attachments that are cosmetic; respawning; footstep audio without direction or distance.

prompts.title: Nier: Automata
prompts.prompt: Build Nier: Automata as a multi-file web action role-playing game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons). The game must SHIFT GENRE continuously and often mid-encounter: the camera drops from third-person action into a fixed top-down twin-stick shooter as the player enters a corridor, flattens into a 2D side-scrolling platformer along a walkway, and becomes a bullet-hell shoot-em-up in flight sections — with the transitions happening live and the controls remaining coherent across all of them. Build the PLUG-IN CHIP system as the game's most distinctive idea: the player has a limited-capacity board into which chips are slotted, and the chips include not only combat modifiers but the INTERFACE ITSELF — the health bar, the minimap, the damage numbers, the enemy markers, the auto-collect and even the operating system chip are all removable components competing for the same space, so a player can free capacity by deleting their own HUD, and removing the OS chip must instantly kill the character and end the run. Structure the campaign as SEQUENTIAL PLAYTHROUGHS rather than replays: the second run retells the same period from a different character with different abilities and information, and later runs continue past it, with the final ending demanding a real sacrifice from the player's saved progress.
prompts.watchFor: A single fixed camera and genre throughout; genre shifts as pre-rendered cutscenes rather than playable; chips as ordinary equipment with the HUD hard-coded and unremovable; an OS chip that cannot be removed or that removing does not kill; the later playthroughs implemented as a new-game-plus with the same content; a final ending with no cost to the player.

prompts.title: Cuphead
prompts.prompt: Build Cuphead as a multi-file web run-and-gun in the style of 1930s rubber-hose animation: every character and object animated as hand-drawn FRAME SEQUENCES with squash, stretch, boil and overshoot, laid over painted watercolour backgrounds, with a big-band and ragtime score and a projector grain over the whole picture. The structure is a BOSS RUSH — the great majority of the game is multi-phase boss encounters rather than levels, and each boss must TRANSFORM completely between phases, changing shape, arena position and attack vocabulary two or three times so that learning it means learning several fights in sequence, with a death returning the player to the start and a progress bar shown on the game-over screen. Build the PARRY as a universal risk-reward verb: anything coloured PINK — a projectile, a platform, a piece of a boss, a hazard — can be parried by pressing jump a second time at the moment of contact with it, which bounces the player upward, negates that threat and charges the super meter, so the safest response to danger is to jump INTO it if it is pink. That must be consistent everywhere and is the acceptance test. Add swappable weapon and charm loadouts chosen between fights, a five-card super meter, an aim-lock, a dash, and a small overworld map with run-and-gun stages between the bosses.
prompts.watchFor: Modern vector or 3D art in place of frame-by-frame hand-drawn animation; bosses that are one long health bar with no transformations; parry restricted to specific scripted objects rather than to everything pink; parries that do not charge the super meter; loadouts that cannot be changed between attempts; a death sequence with load times that break the retry loop; no progress indicator on failure.

prompts.title: Monster Hunter: World
prompts.prompt: Build Monster Hunter: World as a multi-file web co-operative hunting game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons). The monster is an ANIMAL IN AN ECOSYSTEM rather than an encounter, and this is the acceptance test: it must exist in the map before the player arrives, sleeping, feeding, drinking, marking territory and fighting other monsters unprompted, and it must respond to injury the way an animal does — limping, breathing heavily, drooling, retreating to a nest to sleep and recover, or fleeing the zone entirely. Show NO health bar; the player must read its condition entirely from behaviour and from visible damage, because parts BREAK individually — a horn snaps, a tail is severed and remains on the ground as a carveable object, a wing tears — and each break removes a specific attack from its repertoire. Build weapon types as genuinely separate games rather than damage variants: each with its own combo tree, its own movement speed, its own sheathing and commitment, and its own resource layer, so switching weapon means relearning the hunt. Make hunts long, prepared expeditions: study the ecology, lay traps and bombs, use the terrain and other monsters against it, mount it, and carve parts from the corpse to CRAFT the armour and weapons needed for the next tier. Support four-player co-operative hunts with shared carts and a time limit.
prompts.watchFor: A monster that spawns on arrival and stands waiting; a visible health bar, which removes the whole reading-the-animal skill; injury with no limping, fleeing or resting behaviour; parts that cannot be broken or severed, or breaks with no effect on its moveset; fourteen weapons that are the same combo with different numbers; instant hunts with no preparation, traps or terrain use; crafting from generic currency rather than from carved parts.

prompts.title: Return of the Obra Dinn
prompts.prompt: Build Return of the Obra Dinn as a multi-file web deduction game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons) rendered in strict 1-BIT MONOCHROME: real ordered-dither shading computed in screen space over the 3D geometry, so the world is drawn in two colours only and the dithering pattern is stable as the camera moves. The player boards a merchant ship returned to port with its entire crew of sixty dead or missing, carrying a pocket watch that, used on any set of remains, freezes time inside a fully 3D TABLEAU of the exact instant of that person's death — preceded by a few seconds of audio from just before it — which the player then walks around, inspects from any angle and leaves. Tableaux chain: someone visible in one scene has their own remains elsewhere, opening the next. The player fills in a CREW MANIFEST naming every person, their role, and the precise manner and agent of their death, deduced from accents in the audio, clothing, tattoos, bunk assignments, the ship's roster, a group portrait, and who is standing beside whom. The mechanic that makes this rigorous, and the acceptance test, is that the game CONFIRMS ONLY IN GROUPS OF THREE: nothing is validated until three entries are simultaneously correct, so guessing one at a time gives no feedback and the player must build genuine certainty.
prompts.watchFor: Colour or conventional shading instead of screen-space 1-bit dithering, or a dither that swims as the camera moves; tableaux presented as flat images rather than explorable 3D scenes; per-entry confirmation, which reduces the whole game to brute-force guessing; deductions signposted by highlighted clues; a manifest that fills itself in; no audio preceding each scene.

prompts.title: Into the Breach
prompts.prompt: Build Into the Breach as a multi-file web turn-based tactics game on a tiny eight-by-eight grid, with three mechs against insects erupting from the ground. The design is built on PERFECT INFORMATION and it must be total: at the start of every player turn, every enemy on the board displays EXACTLY what it will do — which tile it will attack, for how much damage, and in which direction — with no hidden rolls, no hit percentages and no randomness anywhere in resolution, so each turn is a fully solvable puzzle rather than a gamble. That is the acceptance test. The second inversion is the win condition: the player is not trying to kill the enemies, they are trying to PROTECT the buildings on the grid, since the shared power grid is the only health bar and losing it ends the campaign. Consequently the primary verb is DISPLACEMENT rather than damage — punching, shoving, pulling and dropping enemies so that their telegraphed attack now hits another insect, hits empty ground, or is cancelled by their being moved off their firing line, and so that they are pushed off buildings they were about to strike. Enemies must damage each other when redirected. Add a run structure across islands with mech and pilot upgrades, and on defeat let the player send ONE PILOT back through time into the next run, carrying their experience.
prompts.watchFor: Hidden enemy intentions, hit chances or any random damage roll; a win condition based on killing all enemies rather than protecting buildings; a health pool that is per-unit instead of the shared grid; displacement absent so the only option is damage; redirected attacks that do not hurt other enemies; a large grid, which destroys the puzzle density; no pilot carried between runs.

prompts.title: Subnautica
prompts.prompt: Build Subnautica as a multi-file web underwater survival game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), on an ocean planet after a crash. Progression is GATED BY DEPTH and by breath, which is the whole shape of the game: every excursion is a round trip measured against a finite OXYGEN supply, so the map is explored in expanding rings, and going deeper requires better tanks, then a small submersible, then a larger one, each with a hard CRUSH DEPTH beyond which it takes damage — so the ocean's layers open in a strict order and the pressure of the dark below is always the frontier. Technology is not a tree bought with points: blueprints are unlocked by SCANNING physical fragments of wrecked equipment found scattered on the sea floor, so advancing means exploring, and the acceptance test is that no recipe can be obtained any other way. Add base building with modular rooms, corridors and windows whose HULL INTEGRITY must be reinforced against the depth they are placed at, or they flood. Track oxygen, hunger, thirst and health, with food and water crafted from what is caught and grown. Give the player NO conventional weapons — a knife and defensive tools only — so the large predators are threats to be avoided, distracted or fled rather than killed, and build the deep zones for genuine dread with poor visibility and sound.
prompts.watchFor: A tech tree bought with points rather than blueprints unlocked by scanning fragments in the world; vehicles with no crush depth, letting the player reach the bottom immediately; unlimited oxygen or oxygen that regenerates underwater; base modules with no hull integrity or flooding; conventional weapons that turn predators into ordinary enemies; a flat seabed with no distinct depth layers or biomes; hunger and thirst tracked but trivially satisfied.

prompts.title: Disco Elysium
prompts.prompt: Build Disco Elysium as a multi-file web isometric role-playing game with NO COMBAT SYSTEM AT ALL — every confrontation, including violent ones, is resolved through dialogue and skill checks. The defining invention, and the acceptance test, is that the twenty-four SKILLS ARE CHARACTERS: each one is a voice with its own personality, vocabulary and agenda that INTERJECTS unbidden into the protagonist's internal monologue as a named speaker in the dialogue window — Logic reasoning, Empathy noticing someone's pain, Inland Empire making unhinged intuitive leaps, Electrochemistry begging for drugs, Authority urging him to assert himself — and these voices can be WRONG, can contradict each other, and can push the player toward disaster, so a high skill is not simply better. Build checks as visible dice: two six-sided dice plus the skill plus itemised modifiers against a stated difficulty, with the full arithmetic shown. FAILURE MUST BE CONTENT: a failed white check can be retried after growth, a failed red check is permanent, and both must open different, often better, writing rather than blocking progress. Add the THOUGHT CABINET, where ideas encountered are internalised over real elapsed time to yield a permanent perk with a genuine drawback, and let the player commit to political ideologies with mechanical effects.
prompts.watchFor: A combat system of any kind; skills as passive numbers rather than named speakers that interject with their own voices; skill voices that are always correct; hidden dice rolls or unstated difficulties; failed checks that block progress or simply repeat the same line; no distinction between retryable and permanent checks; a thought cabinet that grants pure bonuses with no drawback; ideologies that are cosmetic labels.

prompts.title: Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice
prompts.prompt: Build Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice as a multi-file web action game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), and invert the usual combat economy. The win condition is not health but POSTURE: both the player and every enemy carry a posture meter that fills when their attacks are blocked or deflected and when they take damage, and when an enemy's posture BREAKS the player lands an instant DEATHBLOW regardless of remaining health. Crucially, posture recovers faster the healthier a character is, so chipping health is only a way of making posture damage stick — the fight is a contest of aggression and rhythm rather than attrition, and running away lets the enemy recover. That relationship is the acceptance test. The core defensive input is the DEFLECT: a block pressed in a tight window as the blow lands, which negates the damage, adds posture to the attacker and rings out — so the correct answer to almost everything is to stand your ground and match the tempo, not to roll away. Build PERILOUS attacks flagged by a warning symbol, each with exactly one correct answer: a thrust countered by stepping into it, a sweep countered by jumping, a grab countered by dodging. Add a grappling hook for vertical traversal, stealth deathblows from above and behind, prosthetic tools, and resurrection on the spot at a cost.
prompts.watchFor: Health as the win condition with posture reduced to a stagger bar; posture that does not regenerate faster at high health, which removes the reason to press the attack; a dodge roll that is a viable universal answer, making deflection optional; a generous or auto-timed parry window; perilous attacks with no distinct counters; no grappling hook or vertical traversal; stealth that cannot produce an instant deathblow.

prompts.title: Resident Evil 2
prompts.prompt: Build the Resident Evil 2 remake as a multi-file web survival horror game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), set in a police station laid out as an interconnected puzzle box rather than a level sequence — locked doors, keys and emblems, and constant backtracking through cleared rooms that never feel safe. The signature mechanic is the STALKER: an unkillable pursuer who ROAMS THE WHOLE BUILDING in real time on his own, tracking the player by SOUND — gunfire, running footsteps, breaking glass — following them between rooms and floors, never despawning and never resetting to a spawn point, so the player's own noise is what summons him and safe rooms are the only respite. He can be staggered and escaped but never beaten, which is the acceptance test. Build SCARCITY into every system: an inventory of a small fixed number of SLOTS where every key item, weapon and herb competes for room, forcing trips to the storage box; ammunition crafted from combined gunpowder types in limited supply; and zombies that require a variable and unpredictable number of headshots, that get back up unless properly destroyed, and that keep the damage inflicted on them permanently, so the player is always deciding whether a corridor is worth clearing at all.
prompts.watchFor: A stalker that appears only in scripted corridors or that despawns after a timer; a pursuer that can be killed; noise having no effect on his tracking; an unlimited or grid-free inventory, which removes all item management; plentiful ammunition, or crafting with no scarcity; zombies that die in a fixed number of shots or that fully respawn; a linear level order with no backtracking or locked-door structure.

prompts.title: Control
prompts.prompt: Build Control as a multi-file web third-person action game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons) with a real rigid-body physics and destruction layer, set in a brutalist government building that houses the paranormal and audits it. That requires the environment to be genuinely destructible and to shed persistent debris, so a long fight leaves an office physically demolished and simultaneously restocks the player's ammunition — which is the acceptance test, since Launch must never run out because the room is always the arsenal. Give the player a single SERVICE WEAPON that reconfigures between forms sharing one regenerating energy pool rather than an arsenal, plus levitation, shield built from held debris, and mind control. Build the building as a metroidvania that RECONFIGURES: shifting corridors, a maze that rearranges, security clearance gates, and areas reached only by levitating. prompts.watchFor: Launch limited to highlighted pickup objects rather than anything loose; an environment that cannot be torn apart when nothing is loose, leaving the player without ammunition; destruction as a decal or a canned animation with no persistent debris; a conventional multi-weapon arsenal instead of one shifting weapon on a shared energy pool; a static level layout with no reconfiguration; story delivered by cutscene rather than collected documents.

prompts.title: Outer Wilds
prompts.prompt: Build Outer Wilds as a multi-file web space exploration game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), set in a tiny hand-made solar system with fully simulated Newtonian ORBITS and gravity, flown in a small ship with real thrust, inertia and no brakes. The structure is a TWENTY-TWO-MINUTE TIME LOOP that ends when the sun goes supernova, after which everything resets to the beginning — and the acceptance test for the entire design is that the ONLY thing that carries over is the player's own KNOWLEDGE. There are no upgrades, no unlocked abilities, no collected items, no levelling and no permanent state of any kind: a player who knew everything could finish the game in one loop from a standing start, and every door in the game is opened by understanding rather than by permission. The second requirement is that the system is DYNAMIC WITHIN THE LOOP: planets physically change as the minutes pass — sand drains out of one world and fills another, burying and exposing different structures; a planet progressively breaks apart; a comet's ice melts as it nears the sun; an anglerfish-filled fog world stays lethal — so a given place is only reachable during a particular window, and knowing WHEN is as important as knowing where. prompts.watchFor: Any persistent unlock, upgrade, item or ability carried between loops, which breaks the entire premise; a door or barrier that opens on progression rather than on knowledge; static planets that do not change during the loop; a loop long enough to remove urgency or too short to reach anywhere; a quest log with objectives instead of a log of facts and open questions; orbital motion faked as a fixed skybox.

prompts.title: Half-Life: Alyx
prompts.prompt: Build Half-Life: Alyx as a multi-file web VR shooter using three.js with WebXR (both vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), with a flat-screen fallback that is explicitly a degraded mode rather than the design target. prompts.watchFor: Reloading on a button press instead of physically inserting a magazine; gravity gloves as an instant pickup with no flick-and-catch arc; a crouch or lean button in place of real body movement; puzzles solved by pressing use rather than by manipulating objects with both hands; any cutscene that takes camera control, which in VR is also nauseating; the flat-screen mode designed first with VR bolted on; CDN-loaded three.js instead of the vendored copy.

prompts.title: Cyberpunk 2077

Build QUICKHACKING as a full combat discipline: the player scans the environment, uploads hacks to enemies, cameras, turrets and vending machines at a RAM cost from a limited pool that regenerates slowly, chaining a blind onto a guard and a short-circuit onto the one behind him, with a breach-protocol code-matrix minigame to weaken a network first. prompts.watchFor: Attributes that only unlock dialogue lines while every level has one physical route; quickhacking without a RAM economy, or hacks usable only on enemies; no breach protocol; cyberware as a flat unlock list with no slots or capacity budget; lifepaths reduced to a different opening cutscene; braindances as a passive video; a city that is wide but not vertical, with interiors that are inaccessible façades.

prompts.title: Microsoft Flight Simulator
prompts.prompt: Build a web flight simulator in the spirit of Microsoft Flight Simulator as a multi-file project using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons). The claim to honour is that the world is THE REAL WORLD, so build the terrain from actual geographic data — a locally bundled regional dataset of real elevation tiles with real coastlines, roads and building footprints rather than the whole planet, since a bundled region is the honest scope for a browser — and generate the scenery procedurally from it: buildings extruded from real footprints, trees placed from land-cover classification, and roads and rivers following their true courses, so a pilot can navigate by recognising the ground beneath them. The second requirement is a genuine FLIGHT MODEL rather than an arcade one: compute lift and drag per control surface from angle of attack and airspeed, model weight, balance, propeller torque and ground effect, and make the aircraft STALL when the wing exceeds its critical angle and enter a spin if it stalls asymmetrically, recoverable only by correct technique. That stall behaviour is the acceptance test. Build a CLICKABLE COCKPIT where every instrument, switch, throttle, trim wheel and radio is operated individually in the panel, add live weather with wind layers and turbulence, and include flight planning with navaids, a moving map and airport approach procedures.
prompts.watchFor: Invented or procedurally noise-generated terrain rather than real geographic data; an arcade flight model that cannot stall or spin; stalls handled as an alarm and an automatic recovery; a cockpit that is a static image with keyboard-only controls; no wind, weather or turbulence affecting the aircraft; no navigation instruments or flight planning; scenery detail that does not correspond to the real place being flown over.

prompts.title: Doom Eternal
prompts.prompt: Build Doom Eternal as a multi-file web first-person shooter using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), and design it as a puzzle box rather than a power fantasy. The engine of the whole thing is a RESOURCE TRIANGLE that must be forced by deliberately tiny carrying capacities: the chainsaw, on a regenerating fuel pip, converts a small enemy into AMMUNITION; the glory kill on a staggered enemy yields HEALTH; and the flame belch, on its own cooldown, sets enemies alight so that damaging them sheds ARMOUR. Ammo capacities must be small enough that no weapon can carry a fight, so the player is compelled to cycle all three systems continuously and combat becomes a rhythm of managing three cooldowns while moving — that compulsion is the acceptance test. Layer on WEAK POINTS as a target-priority puzzle: specific enemies carry destructible components that must be shot off to remove a specific threat — arm cannons blown off one, a shoulder launcher off another, a turret off a third, a shield that must be circled — so the demon roster is a checklist of correct answers rather than a wall of health. prompts.watchFor: Large ammunition reserves, which let a player ignore the chainsaw and collapse the entire loop; glory kills, chainsaw or flame belch producing the wrong resource or all three producing health; no cooldowns, so the systems are free; enemies that are damage sponges with no destructible weak points; a shield or turret enemy killable by shooting it head-on; low mobility with no dash, meat hook or double jump; arenas clearable from one safe position.

prompts.title: Valheim
prompts.prompt: Build Valheim as a multi-file web co-operative survival game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), in a procedurally generated Norse world laid out as concentric BIOMES of escalating danger — meadows, black forest, swamp, mountain, plains — where progression is gated by BOSSES: each biome holds a boss whose defeat drops a power and unlocks the tool tier needed to harvest the next biome's material, so the world opens in a strict, discoverable order rather than by level. Building must be a real STRUCTURAL SIMULATION and this is the acceptance test: every piece has a support value that decreases with distance from the ground and through each connected joint, shown by a colour-coded inspection mode, so a beam extended too far unsupported will visibly weaken and then COLLAPSE, forcing the player to learn about pillars, buttresses and load paths rather than floating blocks in mid-air. prompts.watchFor: Biomes accessible in any order with no boss-gated material tiers; building with no structural integrity so anything can float; food that heals instantly instead of raising maximum health and stamina; unlimited stamina in combat, removing blocks and parries; skills that level from experience rather than use; sailing with no wind direction or tacking; death with no item loss or corpse recovery.

prompts.title: It Takes Two
prompts.prompt: Build It Takes Two as a multi-file web co-operative platformer using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons). It must be MANDATORY two-player co-op with no single-player mode and no AI partner substitute, played in permanent split screen — the whole design assumes two humans who can see each other's view and must talk. The structural commitment, and the acceptance test, is that each chapter gives the two players DIFFERENT, COMPLEMENTARY ABILITIES that are DISCARDED at the end of that chapter and replaced with an entirely new pair: one player gets a nail gun that fires anchors into surfaces while the other gets a hammer that swings from them; one can rewind an object's position in time while the other can spawn a clone of themselves; one shrinks while the other grows; one controls the wind while the other controls fire. Every mechanic must be introduced, explored, escalated and then abandoned within a single chapter, so the game never reuses a verb and the pair are always relearning together. prompts.watchFor: A single-player mode or an AI companion, which removes the entire premise; both players having identical abilities; abilities that persist across the whole game rather than being replaced each chapter; obstacles solvable by one player alone; no split screen, or a shared camera that forces the pair to stay together; chapters that reuse the same verbs with new art.

prompts.title: Forza Horizon 5
prompts.prompt: Build Forza Horizon 5 as a multi-file web open-world racing game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), across a large, varied, sunlit map of desert, jungle, coast, volcano and city. Races are entry points scattered across a WORLD the player drives freely between, not entries in a menu — the drive to the next event is as much the game as the event, so fill the map with speed traps, danger signs, drift zones, smashable boards and cross-country routes that ignore roads entirely. Underneath, build a simulation-grade vehicle model: a tyre model with slip angle and load sensitivity, suspension with real weight transfer under braking and cornering, differential behaviour, drivetrain layout that makes front, rear and all-wheel drive feel distinct, and surface grip that changes on tarmac, dirt, sand and grass. Then layer an ASSIST STACK on top, because the accessibility is deliberate design rather than a compromise: a racing line that colours for braking, traction and stability control, automatic or manual transmission with clutch, braking assist, and a REWIND that steps the simulation back several seconds and lets the player retry a corner — so the same car can be driven by anyone at any level. Add deep tuning of gearing, camber, tyre pressure and aero, plus visual customisation and seasons that change the map.
prompts.watchFor: Arcade handling with uniform grip on every surface and no weight transfer; drivetrain layouts that feel identical; races selected from a menu rather than driven to across a connected world; no rewind, or a rewind that restarts the whole event; assists that cannot be individually toggled; tuning that changes numbers with no perceptible handling effect; a map with only paved routes and no cross-country driving.

prompts.title: Resident Evil Village

Build the inventory as a GRID where every item occupies a specific SHAPE of cells and must be physically arranged and rotated to fit, with the grid expandable by purchase — so managing space is a tactile puzzle and every pickup is a decision. prompts.watchFor: Four regions that play identically with different textures; the doll house letting the player keep their weapons, which removes its entire point; a list inventory instead of a shaped grid requiring arrangement; a grid that never needs managing because it is too large; the merchant selling upgrades with no economy or treasure to find; cooking that gives temporary buffs rather than permanent upgrades; unlimited ammunition or no crafting.

prompts.title: Deathloop

Structure time as a strict grid: FOUR DISTRICTS and FOUR TIME BLOCKS — morning, noon, afternoon, evening — where visiting a district consumes its block and the island advances, so a single loop permits only four visits, and each district is a genuinely different place in each block with different people, different events and different access. Eight targets must ALL die within one single day, and they are never all conveniently placed, so the game is a SCHEDULING PUZZLE: the player must learn each target's routine, find the levers that move them, and engineer convergences — luring one to another's party, sabotaging an event so two attend the same place, triggering a broadcast that draws a third — until a single route through four blocks catches all eight. Make KNOWLEDGE the persistent currency: codes, passwords, routes, documents and leads carry across loops in a structured investigation board, while weapons and powers are LOST on reset unless spent-on and infused with a resource. prompts.watchFor: A free-roaming island with no time-block structure, which removes the entire scheduling puzzle; targets that can be killed across several days instead of within one; targets whose routines cannot be manipulated to converge; knowledge that does not persist, or full gear persistence with no infusion cost; an investigation board that fills itself in; no invasion mode; districts that are identical across the four time blocks.

prompts.title: Elden Ring
prompts.prompt: Build Elden Ring as a multi-file web open-world action role-playing game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), taking stamina-committed Souls combat, runes dropped on death and recoverable once, and checkpoints that respawn all enemies, and opening it into a genuinely free world. The structural rule, and the acceptance test, is that WALKING AWAY IS ALWAYS VALID: no boss, area or region is gated behind another, there are no level requirements and no invisible walls, so a player stuck at any encounter can simply leave in another direction, become stronger elsewhere, and return — the world must be built so that every hard wall has an open alternative. There are NO QUEST MARKERS and no objective list: exploration is driven by what is visible on the horizon and by a guiding light from checkpoints that only ever suggests. The MAP is not given — it is assembled by finding map fragments in each region. Add Ashes of War as swappable weapon skills that can be applied to different weapons, Spirit Ashes that summon an ally as a difficulty lever, huge legacy dungeons built as classic interconnected level design, and asynchronous multiplayer messages, invasions and co-operative summons.
prompts.watchFor: Level or progression gates on regions, which negates the freedom the design rests on; quest markers or an objective waypoint; a full map given from the start rather than assembled from fragments; a horse that cannot double jump or use updraughts, flattening the world; Ashes of War locked to specific weapons; open-world content that is entirely procedural filler with no hand-built legacy dungeons; no asynchronous multiplayer traces.

prompts.title: God of War (PC Release)
prompts.prompt: Build God of War as a multi-file web third-person action game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), retelling Norse myth as a father and son on a journey. The technical and directorial commitment that defines it, and the acceptance test for the build, is the SINGLE UNBROKEN SHOT: there is not one camera cut in the entire game — no cuts between gameplay and cutscene, no cuts within cutscenes, no cut on death, no cut when opening a menu — so the camera is one continuous take from the first frame to the last, and every transition, every loading moment and every death must be designed to be traversed by a moving camera rather than hidden by an edit. This forces a close over-the-shoulder camera, which in turn requires OFF-SCREEN THREAT INDICATORS that show the direction of attacks the player cannot see. The signature weapon is an axe that is THROWN and then RECALLED: it sticks in enemies and scenery, freezes what it hits, can be used to pin an enemy or hold a mechanism open, and on recall FLIES BACK THROUGH everything between it and the player, so throw placement and recall line are both tactical choices. prompts.watchFor: Any camera cut, including on death, on menu open or between gameplay and cutscenes; a distant camera that removes the need for off-screen indicators; an axe that is thrown but not recalled, or a recall that teleports it rather than flying it back through enemies; a freeze effect with no tactical use; a companion who is invulnerable scenery with no commands; disconnected levels rather than interconnected gated realms.

prompts.title: Neon White
prompts.prompt: Build Neon White as a multi-file web first-person speedrunning platformer using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons). The mechanic the entire game is built from, and the acceptance test, is that CARDS ARE BOTH WEAPON AND MOVEMENT: each card picked up is a gun with limited shots, but it can instead be DISCARDED to perform a traversal move unique to that card — one discards into a double jump, one into a horizontal dash that passes through obstacles, one into a grappling hook that yanks the player to a target, one into a vertical rocket, one into a ground-slam that also damages. So ammunition and mobility are the same finite resource, and every level is an argument about whether a card is worth more as a bullet or as a jump. Levels must be SHORT — twenty to sixty seconds — cleared of demons on a timer, with medal thresholds from bronze to ace, an instant restart on a single key with no loading whatsoever, and a persistent leaderboard. Crucially, the intended route is not the optimal one: every level must hide shortcuts, skips and card-sequence tricks that only reveal themselves on replay, and a hint system should gesture at a secret without showing it. Wrap it in a stylised heaven-and-hell visual novel between missions with gift-giving side objectives hidden in the levels.
prompts.watchFor: Cards that are only weapons with a separate movement button, which collapses the whole resource tension; discards that all perform the same move; levels long enough that a restart is a punishment; any loading pause on restart; no medal tiers or timer; a single intended route with no discoverable shortcuts, so replaying is pointless; the between-mission story mode gating levels behind unskippable text.

prompts.title: Baldur's Gate 3
prompts.prompt: Build Baldur's Gate 3 as a multi-file web role-playing game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), running honest fifth-edition D&D rules in TURN-BASED combat: an action, a bonus action, a movement allowance and REACTIONS that trigger on an opponent's turn, advantage and disadvantage, concentration on spells that breaks when the caster is hit, spell slots recovered on rest, and every roll shown as a die on screen with its modifiers and the option to spend inspiration on a reroll. The quality that must be built structurally, and the acceptance test, is REACTIVITY WITHOUT GUARDRAILS: any NPC in the game can be killed, including quest givers and merchants, and the game must ROUTE AROUND IT rather than blocking the attack or failing the run — the quest resolves another way, someone else picks it up, or a consequence lands later. In the same spirit the world must accept unintended solutions: shoving an enemy off a cliff, stacking crates to reach a ledge, casting grease and igniting it, talking to an animal for information, disguising as another race to pass a checkpoint, throwing a party member across a chasm, or pushing a chandelier onto a crowd. Add fully performed cinematic dialogue, playable origin characters with their own histories, approval-driven companions, and four-player drop-in co-op where players may split up and act against each other.
prompts.watchFor: Essential NPCs made unkillable or attacks on them blocked, which breaks the central promise; reactions, concentration or advantage omitted from the rules; hidden dice rolls; environmental interactions restricted to marked objects; a single correct solution per encounter; companions with approval that gates nothing; co-op where all players must stay in one conversation or one location.

prompts.title: Alan Wake 2
prompts.prompt: Build Alan Wake 2 as a multi-file web survival horror game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), told through TWO PROTAGONISTS in two interleaved stories the player switches between at will from a safe room, each with their own map, their own inventory and their own distinct mechanic. The detective's mechanic is the MIND PLACE: a private mental room the player enters at any moment, holding a case board where collected evidence is pinned and must be manually DRAGGED onto the correct question to form a deduction, plus a profiling chair for interrogating suspects in absentia — so investigation is an explicit action the player performs rather than something that resolves itself. The writer's mechanic is the PLOT BOARD, and it is the acceptance test: he is trapped in a place shaped by story, and choosing a scene on his board REWRITES THE WORLD AROUND HIM — the same street physically changes its layout, lighting, occupants and available routes depending on which scene is currently written, so the level itself is the variable the player edits. Keep the flashlight as a weapon that must burn away a shadow shield before bullets do anything, ration batteries and ammunition, and mix live-action video and musical sequences into the game as first-class scenes.
prompts.watchFor: One protagonist, or a switch that is a chapter break rather than a player choice; a case board that fills itself in or that only requires clicking through; a plot board that changes dialogue but not the level geometry, routes and occupants; enemies killable without first burning off their shadow shield; unlimited batteries; the two campaigns sharing one map and inventory; live-action and musical sequences omitted as gimmicks.

prompts.title: Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty
prompts.prompt: Build Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty as a multi-file web spy-thriller expansion campaign using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), set in a walled-off, war-damaged district that is denser, more vertical and more hostile than the surrounding city. The narrative engine, and the acceptance test, is DIVIDED LOYALTY: the player works simultaneously for two handlers whose accounts of each other are irreconcilable, each drip-feeding information that reframes the other, and at a defined point the player must COMMIT to one, irreversibly, without ever being given enough evidence to be sure. That fork must lead to genuinely different final acts with different locations and different casts, and it must also change the ending available in the base campaign, so the expansion reaches back into the main game. Around it, rebuild progression: replace flat cyberware slot counts with a CYBERWARE CAPACITY budget that every implant draws from, so builds are a constrained allocation; add a relic skill tree unlocked by finding fragments; and overhaul the police into a staged pursuit with responders, road blocks, helicopters and pursuit vehicles that can be lost by breaking line of sight. Add vehicle combat with mounted weapons and drive-by shooting, airdrops of gear, and a district with its own faction economy.
prompts.watchFor: A single handler, or a betrayal fork that is signposted with an obviously trustworthy party; the choice reversible or made at a save-scummable prompt with no commitment; branches that share the same final act with different dialogue; no effect on the base game's ending; cyberware still limited by slot counts rather than a shared capacity budget; police that spawn behind the player and never pursue properly; vehicle combat missing.

prompts.title: Lethal Company
prompts.prompt: Build Lethal Company as a multi-file web co-operative horror game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), where a crew of underpaid contractors scavenges scrap from abandoned industrial moons. The mechanic that makes it work, and the acceptance test, is PROXIMITY VOICE CHAT: players hear each other only when physically near, with volume falling off over distance and muffled through walls, so getting separated genuinely means being alone, and panicked shouting carries only as far as it would. Walkie-talkies extend that range but cost a HAND SLOT and broadcast the holder's voice out loud into whatever room they are standing in, which can get them killed. Build asymmetric roles from the ship itself: one player can stay aboard at the TERMINAL, reading a radar of the facility, watching helmet cameras, opening and closing security doors remotely and calling out warnings — playing an entirely different game from the crew inside. Impose a QUOTA that rises every cycle: the crew must sell enough scrap by the deadline or all of them are terminated and the run ends. Make players fragile, slow and permanently dead for the run, with corpses that must be carried back to the ship to be worth anything. Give creatures rules that must be learned by dying — one that only moves when unobserved, one that hunts by sound, one that is harmless until touched.
prompts.watchFor: Global voice chat, which removes the isolation the game is built from; walkie-talkies with no hand cost or no local broadcast; a terminal that is a map screen rather than a distinct role with door control and cameras; a fixed quota that never escalates; respawning during a run; corpses that need not be recovered; monsters with generic chase behaviour instead of specific learnable rules.

prompts.title: Dave the Diver
prompts.prompt: Build Dave the Diver as a multi-file web genre mashup structured around a strict DAY CYCLE where the two halves feed each other and neither works alone. In the morning the player DIVES: a 2D side-scrolling descent into a procedurally regenerated undersea trench that is different every day, governed by a finite OXYGEN gauge and a weight-limited cargo hold, where fish are harpooned and speared, hazards and predators must be avoided, and going deeper for rarer species means less air for the climb back. In the evening the player RUNS A SUSHI RESTAURANT, and the acceptance test is that the fish caught that morning ARE the menu — the exact species and quantities in the cargo hold become the available dishes, so a bad dive is a bad service. Serve customers in a timed real-time rush by pouring tea, carrying plates and refilling wasabi, set prices per dish, hire and train staff with their own skills, and invest the profits in better harpoons, bigger tanks, faster boats and kitchen upgrades that make the next dive deeper and the next service larger. Add fish farming, a weapons researcher, cooking minigames, and story episodes that interrupt the loop with set-piece dives.
prompts.watchFor: The two halves disconnected, with the restaurant stocked from a shop rather than from the morning's actual catch; unlimited oxygen or cargo capacity; a hand-authored trench that is identical each day; restaurant service that resolves automatically instead of being played in real time; upgrades that do not visibly extend dive depth or service capacity; no staff, pricing or farming layer.

prompts.title: Helldivers 2
prompts.prompt: Build Helldivers 2 as a multi-file web four-player co-operative shooter using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), played as expendable troopers in an aggressively cheerful propaganda war. FRIENDLY FIRE IS ALWAYS ON and cannot be disabled, which is the foundation: every orbital strike, sentry turret, grenade and reload is as dangerous to the squad as to the enemy, so the game is fundamentally about not killing your own team while panicking. The signature system, and the acceptance test, is the STRATAGEM: calling anything down from orbit — an airstrike, a supply drop, a turret, a heavy weapon, a reinforcement — requires the player to input a specific DIRECTIONAL CODE SEQUENCE, several arrow presses long, memorised per stratagem and typed WHILE MOVING AND UNDER FIRE, with a mistake cancelling the input. This turns support fire into a performance under pressure, and the codes must be genuinely memorised rather than picked from a menu. Then throw the beacon, which physically lands and can be kicked, dropped in the wrong place or stuck to an enemy. Build missions procedurally on large maps with objectives and a countdown extraction under escalating pressure, ammunition and stims that must be resupplied, ragdoll physics, and a persistent GALACTIC WAR where every player's mission results feed one shared, visibly moving front line.
prompts.watchFor: Friendly fire disabled or reduced to a token; stratagems selected from a menu or wheel instead of typed as directional codes; code entry that pauses the game or cannot be interrupted; beacons that teleport their payload rather than physically landing where thrown; a fixed set of hand-authored missions; no shared persistent war state across players; ammunition that regenerates, removing the resupply loop.

prompts.title: Metaphor: ReFantazio
prompts.prompt: Build Metaphor: ReFantazio as a multi-file web turn-based role-playing game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), in a fantasy world built around prejudice between tribes and a public race for the throne. The structural pressure, and the acceptance test, is the CALENDAR: the game runs on dated days counting down to fixed political deadlines, each day offers only a small number of time slots, and every slot spent is a slot lost — so advancing the dungeon, deepening a bond with a follower, studying to raise a personal virtue, or taking a job are mutually exclusive uses of the same finite day, and a player cannot do everything before the deadline arrives. Build ARCHETYPES as the class system: each party member equips an archetype with its own skills, statistics and appearance, archetypes advance along lineage trees, skills learned on one can be INHERITED and carried onto another, and the tiers a character can access are gated by their bond rank with the corresponding follower — tying the social calendar directly to combat power. Blend the combat layers: weak enemies are dispatched in a real-time action swing in the field with no encounter at all, while real fights drop into full turn-based battle with press-turn style bonuses for hitting weaknesses, a front and rear row, and synthesis attacks between characters.
prompts.watchFor: An untimed campaign where every activity can be completed, which removes all exclusion; deadlines that slip or that the game waits for; archetypes as fixed classes with no inheritance or lineage tree; archetype tiers unlocked by level rather than by follower bonds; all combat forced into turn-based encounters with no real-time field layer; no weakness or press-turn system; followers whose bonds grant only flavour scenes.

prompts.title: Animal Well
prompts.prompt: Build Animal Well as a multi-file web 2D metroidvania rendered in dense pixel art with real dynamic lighting, soft shadows, reflections and a CRT-style presentation, set in a strange dark warren with no text, no dialogue, no tutorial, no objective markers and no explanation of anything. The design principle, and the acceptance test, is that the items are NOT upgrades but TOOLS WITH EMERGENT USES: a slinky, a bubble wand, a frisbee, a yo-yo, a flute, a top. Each must have several genuinely different applications that the game never states — the bubble wand blows a bubble that is a temporary platform, and also a light source, and also a distraction for a creature, and also a way to carry an object upward — and progression must come from the player REALISING a use rather than from being granted permission. No item may be a simple double jump or a coloured key. Build a large interconnected map with no fast-travel handholding, animals that are hazards with specific behaviours rather than enemies to be killed, and no combat system at all. Layer the secrets: beyond the ordinary ending there must be a second and then a third stratum of puzzles hidden in the world's geometry, art and audio, deliberately obscure enough to reward exhaustive study and note-taking rather than reflexes.
prompts.watchFor: Text tutorials, dialogue or objective markers, all of which break the wordless design; items that are conventional traversal upgrades or keys with a single use; tool uses that are signposted rather than discovered; a combat system with health and attacks; a single ending with no deeper layers of secrets; flat lighting with no dynamic shadows; a linear area order that removes the interconnection.

prompts.title: Dragon's Dogma 2
prompts.prompt: Build Dragon's Dogma 2 as a multi-file web open-world action role-playing game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons). The system that defines it, and the acceptance test, is the PAWN: AI companions who genuinely LEARN. A pawn that has fought a particular monster several times must remember its weak point and then say so unprompted in a later fight; a pawn that has completed a quest in another world must know where the objective is and physically RUN AHEAD to lead the player there rather than pointing at a marker; and pawns are hired from other players' worlds, arriving with whatever knowledge they accumulated elsewhere, so their expertise is imported rather than scripted. Build the second pillar as physical CLIMBING: large monsters are terrain, and the player can grab on, scale them while they thrash and buck, hang from a limb and strike a weak point that cannot be reached from the ground, with stamina draining the whole time. Deliberately withhold convenient fast travel so that CROSSING THE WORLD is the game — night is genuinely dark and dangerous and requires a lantern with fuel, and journeys are interrupted by ambushes, collapsing bridges and oxcarts that can be attacked. Add vocations with distinct movesets, physics-driven emergent moments like carrying an NPC or throwing a pawn, and permanent consequences for NPC deaths.
prompts.watchFor: Pawns as generic followers with no accumulated knowledge or spoken hints; pawns that point at a quest marker instead of leading; no cross-world pawn hiring; monsters that cannot be climbed, or climbing that is a scripted quick-time event; unlimited fast travel, which erases the journey; nights that are lit well enough not to need a lantern; NPC deaths that are undone or prevented.

prompts.title: Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2
prompts.prompt: Build Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 as a multi-file web third-person action shooter using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), playing an armoured giant against an endless alien swarm. The technical claim, and the acceptance test, is SCALE: hundreds to thousands of enemies must be on screen at once as a physical tide with real movement, mass and crowd pathing — flowing around obstacles, climbing over each other, funnelling through gaps — rather than a handful of enemies in front of a crowd sprite or a scrolling backdrop. That demands instanced rendering, level-of-detail and a flow-field or steering approach to pathing at scale. The combat economy must then push the player INTO that tide rather than away from it: health is a small pool, but ARMOUR sits over it and is restored ONLY by landing melee EXECUTIONS on staggered enemies and by successful PARRIES, so retreating to cover means dying with no armour while wading in and killing restores it. Build the GUN STRIKE as the connective tissue: a well-timed parry opens the enemy and triggers a point-blank pistol shot that also restores armour. Add ranged and melee weapon families with distinct handling, three-player co-operative campaign play with classes and perks, and a separate wave-defence mode.
prompts.watchFor: A dozen enemies at a time presented as a swarm; crowds rendered as a static backdrop or as sprites with no pathing or collision; regenerating health or cover-based recovery, which reverses the intended aggression; armour restored by pickups rather than by executions and parries; no gun strike, or a parry with no follow-up; melee and ranged weapons that all handle the same; no co-operative mode.

prompts.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
prompts.prompt: Build Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 as a multi-file web turn-based role-playing game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), in a melancholy belle-époque world where a painted number on a monolith decides who dies each year. The combat is turn-based on the player's turn and an ACTION GAME on the enemy's, and that hybrid is the acceptance test: when an enemy attacks, the player must respond in REAL TIME to each individual blow in the combo — parrying within a tight window, dodging, or jumping over a low sweep — with a perfect parry chain building toward a devastating counter-attack, so no incoming damage is ever unavoidable and a skilled player can take a whole boss turn without a scratch. Enemy attack sequences must be authored with distinct, learnable rhythms including deliberate delays that bait an early press. On the player's turn, layer free AIM shots into weak points on top of standard actions and a stain or charge mechanic that rewards planning several turns ahead. Build the PICTOS system for growth: equipped items grant passive effects, and after a character has fought several battles with one equipped, that effect is LEARNED PERMANENTLY as a Lumina that can be re-equipped freely with a point budget, so builds are assembled from what the party has actually used.
prompts.watchFor: Enemy turns resolved by a damage roll with no timed defensive input, which discards the entire hook; a single generic parry window shared by every attack; attack patterns with uniform timing and no baiting delays; no free-aim layer on the player's turn; Pictos that grant effects only while equipped, with no permanent learning; a learned-ability budget large enough to equip everything at once.

prompts.title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance II
prompts.prompt: Build Kingdom Come: Deliverance II as a multi-file web historical open-world role-playing game using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), set in medieval Bohemia with NO magic, no dragons and no fantasy of any kind — the constraint is the identity. Skills improve strictly BY USE. The system that must be built and is the acceptance test is APPEARANCE AS A SOCIAL STATE: clothing is tracked in layers over the body, each garment has its own condition, cleanliness and charisma, and dirt and BLOOD accumulate visibly on them from travel and combat — so an NPC reacts to a player who is well dressed and clean quite differently from one who is spattered and filthy, guards will stop and question a bloodied stranger, and a witness can later identify someone by what they were wearing. Washing, mending and changing clothes therefore become real preparation. Build sword fighting as a directional system: a hit-zone rose selects the direction of each strike, blocks must match the incoming direction, master strikes are timed counters, weapons have distinct reach and stamina cost, and armour is layered so a blade that cannot penetrate mail must find a gap. prompts.watchFor: Any magical or fantastical element; skills that level from experience points rather than use; clothing as a flat armour value with no layers, condition, cleanliness or blood; NPCs who react identically regardless of the player's appearance; lock-on hack-and-slash combat with no directional strikes, matched blocks or master strikes; armour as one number ignoring layers and gaps; alchemy resolved by a crafting menu; unlimited free saving.

prompts.title: Hades 2
prompts.prompt: Build Hades 2 as a multi-file web isometric action roguelike, keeping the run-based structure of chambers with a choice of exits, stacking divine boons that combine into wildly different builds, duo boons that only appear when two specific gods are both present, and a story that advances continuously through both victories and deaths with characters reacting to what just happened. This sequel's own systems must be the focus. First, MAGICK: a second resource alongside health that gates OMEGA versions of every action — hold the attack, special, cast or dash input to spend magick on a charged, larger, slower variant — so every input in the game has two forms and the player is constantly deciding whether they can afford the better one, with boons that alter Omega variants specifically. That dual-input economy is the acceptance test. Second, a GATHERING and INCANTATION meta layer: runs yield materials harvested from the world with specific tools — herbs, ore, fish, silver — which are spent at a cauldron on permanent incantations that unlock new regions, mechanics, weapons and characters, so between-run progress is a resource-management game rather than a currency counter.
