prompts.watchFor: No magick resource, or Omega moves on cooldowns rather than a spendable pool; Omega variants that are simply stronger with no trade-off in speed or cost; boons that stack additively with no duos or build identity; a between-run shop that spends a single generic currency instead of gathered materials and incantations; one direction of travel; narrative that only advances on a win; a fixed weapon with no aspects.

prompts.title: Split Fiction
prompts.prompt: Build Split Fiction as a multi-file web co-operative action platformer using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons). It is MANDATORY two-player co-op with no single-player mode and no AI partner, in permanent split screen, and the framing is that two writers are trapped inside their own stories — so the game alternates between a hard SCIENCE-FICTION world and a high FANTASY world, and each player's abilities are drawn from the world they belong to and are swapped or reassigned as the pair cross between them. Every chapter must introduce a NEW pair of complementary abilities, explore and escalate them, then discard them — one player gets a grappling data-tether while the other gets a gravity inverter; one becomes a dragon while the other rides; one can phase through matter while the other solidifies it — and every significant obstacle must require both simultaneously. Use the SPLIT SCREEN itself as a design element rather than a necessity: let the two frames show different scales, different points in time, or different versions of the same room, and let the dividing line move, rotate and be crossed. prompts.watchFor: A single-player mode or AI partner; identical abilities for both players; abilities that persist across the whole game instead of being replaced each chapter; obstacles either player can solve alone; a shared camera instead of split screen, or a split screen that is never used as a design device; side stories omitted; the two worlds differing only in art with the same mechanics.

prompts.title: Doom: The Dark Ages
prompts.prompt: Build Doom: The Dark Ages as a multi-file web first-person shooter using three.js (vendored locally, core only — no examples/jsm add-ons), and deliberately INVERT the design of its predecessor: where that game was about jumping and dodging, this one is about standing your ground. README must explain trusted HTTPS hosting on Quest (plain LAN HTTP is insufficient), controls, comfort and a manual headset checklist. Include real goals, results and restart, not just a VR scene.
prompts.watchFor: Enemies that walk off the path or clip through each other; tower targeting that ignores range or priority; splash damage hitting only one target; flyers following the road; thrown boulders that inherit no hand velocity or pass through the table; scaling the table that desynchronises enemy positions from the road; gold that can go negative. Also check real stereo immersive-vr on Quest 3, both tracked controllers, in-world menus, desktop fallback, HTTPS errors, recenter, pause and exit/re-enter; desktop preview alone cannot verify headset compatibility.

prompts.title: Frontier Lab — Race to Superintelligence
prompts.prompt: Build a strategy-management game as a multi-file web game (index.html + JS + CSS + README) where the player runs an AI research lab and the goal is to be first to build a superintelligence — and to make it aligned. Core loop in weekly turns or pausable real time: buy or rent compute (GPU generations with price/performance improving over time, datacentres constrained by power contracts and cooling), hire researchers and engineers from a talent market with specialisms (pretraining, RL, infra, interpretability, alignment), gather and license data, then design training runs by choosing parameter count, tokens and compute budget. Model outcomes with a scaling-law formula (loss falls as a power law in compute, with a compute-optimal parameters-to-tokens ratio that rewards the player for balancing them) plus random research breakthroughs that shift the curve. Map loss to benchmark capability scores and an overall capability level on a ladder from chatbot to AGI to superintelligence. Fund everything by shipping products (API, consumer app, enterprise deals) whose revenue depends on capability and reliability, and by raising funding rounds that dilute control. Run rival labs as AI opponents with their own strategies and press releases, plus events: GPU export controls, a data-licensing lawsuit, a key researcher poached, a model jailbreak scandal, new regulation that requires evaluations before deployment. A separate alignment track (interpretability, evals, oversight) must keep pace with capability: crossing each capability threshold triggers a safety evaluation, and reaching superintelligence with alignment lagging ends in a bad ending. Endings: aligned superintelligence (win), misaligned takeover, bankruptcy, a rival getting there first, or being shut down by regulators. Include a research tech tree, charts of loss vs compute and capability vs alignment over time, a news feed, save/load, and a difficulty setting.
prompts.watchFor: Capability that rises linearly with money spent (no power-law scaling or compute-optimal trade-off); an alignment track that is a cosmetic bar with no effect on the ending; rivals that never act; revenue independent of capability; unbounded exponential growth that makes the game trivially won by mid-game; no failure states.

prompts.title: Final Approach — Runway Landing Challenge
prompts.prompt: Build a 3D runway-landing game as a multi-file web game (index.html + JS + CSS + README) using the provisioned three.js core at lib/three.min.js (no examples/jsm add-ons, no external assets; build all meshes procedurally). The player picks one of three aircraft with genuinely different flight models: a four-engine jumbo jet (heavy inertia, slow engine spool-up, flaps and gear, spoilers and reverse thrust, approach around 150 knots, tail strike risk if over-rotated in the flare), a single-engine light aircraft (low stall speed, strong crosswind sensitivity, propwash, landing on a short grass or tarmac strip), and a military jet (high approach speed, high angle-of-attack approach, afterburner go-around, drag chute, optional carrier-style arrestor-wire landing). Implement a simple but coherent flight model: lift and drag from angle of attack and airspeed with a stall, thrust with spool time, pitch/roll/yaw inertia, ground effect near the runway, and wheel/ground contact with braking and friction. Each scenario starts on approach several miles out; the runway has centreline and edge lights, approach lights, PAPI lights and an ILS glideslope/localiser shown on the HUD. Add wind and gusts, crosswind, rain, low cloud and night variants. Score the landing on touchdown zone, sink rate, centreline deviation, bank angle, remaining speed and stopping distance, with grades from Butter to Crash; forgetting the gear or flaps must have consequences. Include chase, cockpit and tower cameras, keyboard/mouse and gamepad controls, a go-around option, a career of progressively harder airports and weather, and replay of the last landing from the tower camera.
prompts.watchFor: Aircraft that fly on rails with no stall or energy management; all three aircraft handling identically; the ground as a flat kill plane with no gear contact; PAPI lights that don't change colour with glidepath; crosswind with no drift; landings scored only as survive/crash; physics tied to frame rate.

prompts.title: Tranquility — 3D Lunar Landing
prompts.prompt: Build a 3D lunar landing game as a multi-file web game (index.html + JS + CSS + README) using the provisioned three.js core at lib/three.min.js (no examples/jsm add-ons, no external assets; build all meshes procedurally). The player flies an Apollo-style lunar module down to the barren Moon: black sky, a single harsh sun producing long sharp shadows, Earth hanging over the horizon, and a procedurally generated regolith surface with craters of many sizes, boulder fields and rilles, so picking a safe spot is part of the challenge. Model one-sixth gravity, a throttleable descent engine with limited fuel whose mass changes the craft's inertia, and RCS thrusters for full 3-axis attitude control plus translation, with an optional attitude-hold assist. Show a HUD/instrument panel with altitude above ground from a landing radar, vertical and horizontal velocity, a cross-pointer for horizontal drift, attitude, fuel with 60- and 30-second bingo callouts, and the contact-light when the probes touch. As the engine nears the surface, kick up a sheet of dust that obscures the ground. Judge touchdown by vertical speed, horizontal speed, tilt and whether the legs rest on a slope or boulder; allow an abort that stages to the ascent engine. Provide several landing sites (flat mare, crater rim, highland boulder field, polar shadowed crater with low sun), cameras from the window, chase and a ground view, a descent profile chart after each landing, and scores for precision to a target marker and fuel left.
prompts.watchFor: Earth-like gravity or atmosphere-like drag; the craft rotating by setting angles directly instead of torque and angular momentum; altitude measured from zero height instead of the terrain below; landing on a boulder or 20° slope scored as safe; flat terrain with painted-on craters; fuel not affecting mass; no dust or shadow cues so depth is unreadable.

prompts.title: Mayor — City Simulation
prompts.prompt: Build a city-building simulation as a multi-file web game (index.html + JS + CSS + README) in the spirit of the original SimCity, top-down on Canvas. On a 64×64 map with terrain, the player lays roads, power lines and plants, and zones Residential, Commercial and Industrial land that only grows when road-connected and powered. Drive growth from RCI demand meters that respond to the jobs/population balance; land value from pollution, crime and parks; police and fire coverage radii. Run a monthly budget with tax sliders, maintenance and a treasury. Add overlays (power, pollution, land value, crime, traffic), speed controls, disasters (spreading fire, tornado), and save/load. Make it a game: scenarios with goals and deadlines (reach 50,000 population in 20 years, fix a polluted industrial town, rebuild after an earthquake), a mayor approval rating that can get the player voted out, and bankruptcy as a fail state, plus a free sandbox.
prompts.watchFor: Zones growing without roads or power; power connectivity recomputed every frame; demand meters that never respond to jobs vs population; overlays with no underlying field; no scenario goals or fail states.

prompts.title: Gaia — Planet Simulation
prompts.prompt: Build a planet-scale simulation game as a multi-file web game (index.html + JS + CSS + README) in the spirit of SimEarth. A wrap-around world map tracks elevation, temperature, rainfall and biome per cell, with an energy balance from latitude-dependent sunlight, ice/cloud albedo, CO₂ greenhouse strength and heat diffusion, so an ice-albedo feedback can tip the planet into a snowball or runaway greenhouse. Life spreads and evolves through eras toward intelligence based on habitability. The player spends limited energy points on god-powers: raise/lower terrain, seed life, adjust CO₂, trigger volcanoes or meteor strikes. Include map layers, time-series charts and a speed control spanning millions of years. Make it a game: scenarios such as terraforming Mars, surviving a brightening sun, or thawing a snowball Earth, each with a goal (sustain a civilisation to the space age) and failure (planet becomes uninhabitable).
prompts.watchFor: No latitude gradient; missing ice-albedo feedback so nothing tips; biomes from temperature alone; no east-west wrap; unlimited god powers so there's no challenge.

prompts.title: London Bus Driver
prompts.prompt: Build a London bus driving game as a multi-file web game (index.html + JS + CSS + README) using the provisioned three.js core at lib/three.min.js (no examples/jsm add-ons, no external assets; build all meshes procedurally). Drive a red double-decker on the LEFT side of the road through a procedurally generated London street grid with terraces, zebra crossings, traffic lights, black cabs, cyclists and pedestrians. The route has numbered stops: pull in close to the kerb, open doors, and passengers walk to board or alight, taking time proportional to headcount. The bus has a long wheelbase with rear-axle steering geometry, weight-dependent acceleration and braking, and a tail that swings wide on corners. Score punctuality against a timetable, passenger comfort (penalise harsh braking and cornering g-force), and fines for red lights, kerb strikes and missed stops. Include chase, cab and top-deck cameras, a HUD (speed, next stop, schedule delta, passengers), a minimap, several routes with rush hour and night variants, and a shift-end report card.
prompts.watchFor: Driving on the right; steering pivoting around the bus centre; AI traffic driving through the bus or ignoring lights; passengers teleporting aboard; no timetable pressure.

prompts.title: Fed Chair — Monetary Policy Game
prompts.prompt: Build a turn-based economic strategy game as a multi-file web game (index.html + JS + CSS + README) where the player is chair of the Federal Reserve. Each turn is an FOMC meeting: set the policy rate in 25bp steps, choose balance-sheet policy (QE/hold/QT) and a forward-guidance statement. Run a small New-Keynesian model: an IS curve with lagged effect of real rates on the output gap, an expectations-augmented Phillips curve, inflation expectations that de-anchor as credibility falls, Okun's-law unemployment, and markets (bond yields, stock index) that react to surprises versus expectations. Random shocks (oil spike, bank run, pandemic, productivity boom) arrive with news headlines. Show a Taylor-rule benchmark, charts of inflation, unemployment, GDP, rates and credibility, plus congressional testimony events with multiple-choice answers. The player wins a second term by keeping the dual mandate on target; being fired, a recession spiral or runaway inflation ends the game, with an end-of-term grade.
prompts.watchFor: Rates affecting inflation instantly; markets reacting to rate level rather than surprise; credibility with no effect on expectations; Taylor rule with a wrong-signed output gap; no losing condition.

prompts.title: Trading Floor — Stock Market Game
prompts.prompt: Build a stock-trading game as a multi-file web game (index.html + JS + CSS + README). Eight fictional tickers follow geometric Brownian motion with sector correlation, volatility clustering and news-driven jumps. Show a candlestick chart with timeframes, volume, moving averages and RSI, a Level-2 order book and time-and-sales tape from simulated participants. The player starts with $100,000 and places market, limit and stop orders, goes long or short, and can use 2× margin with margin calls. Track positions, average cost, realised/unrealised P&L, fees and an equity curve versus the index. Make it a game: career levels with targets (beat the index by 5% this quarter, survive a crash, don't exceed a drawdown limit), an insider-tip event that tempts the player into an investigation, a leaderboard, and a performance report with Sharpe ratio and max drawdown.
prompts.watchFor: Negative prices; limit orders filling at the limit when price gapped through; wrong-signed short P&L; candles from a single tick; unannualised Sharpe; margin calls that never trigger.

prompts.title: Headteacher — School Management Game
prompts.prompt: Build a school management game as a multi-file web game (index.html + JS + CSS + README) where the player is the new headteacher. A top-down floor plan shows classrooms, hall, playground, canteen and staff room, with students and teachers walking between rooms on the bell timetable. Students have ability, motivation, wellbeing, attendance and friendships; teachers have subject, skill, energy and morale. The player hires staff within a budget, builds the timetable, sets class sizes, invests in facilities, and picks policies (homework, uniform, clubs, anti-bullying) that trade grades against wellbeing and burnout. Events: illness, a resignation, a parent complaint, a surprise inspection grading attainment, behaviour and leadership. Progress through terms and years with exam results and league-table position driving next year's applications and funding. Win by turning a failing school into an Outstanding one within five years; lose if the governors remove you.
prompts.watchFor: Students who never move on the bell; a teacher in two rooms at once; policies that change a number with no effect on individuals; an inspection that ignores simulated metrics; no win or lose.

prompts.title: Outbreak Response
prompts.prompt: Build an epidemic response game as a multi-file web game (index.html + JS + CSS + README). Hundreds of agents commute between homes, workplaces, schools and shops across a town; infection depends on proximity and exposure time, following an SEIR model with a hidden asymptomatic fraction. The player is the public-health director with a limited budget and public-trust meter: deploy testing, contact tracing, masks, school closures, lockdowns and a vaccine that arrives mid-game with a daily capacity. Compliance falls as restrictions drag on. Show S/E/I/R/D stacked area charts, effective R, hospital occupancy against capacity, an infection heat map and an economic cost panel. Scenarios (flu, measles, novel pandemic) end with a score balancing deaths, economic damage and trust; overwhelming the hospital or losing all trust is a loss.
prompts.watchFor: Infection at any distance; R₀ not calibrating transmission; interventions with no delay or compliance decay; no trade-off between health and economy; unbounded chart arrays.

prompts.title: Wild Balance — Ecosystem Game
prompts.prompt: Build an ecosystem game as a multi-file web game (index.html + JS + CSS + README). Grass, rabbits and foxes live on a 2D landscape; creatures have energy, age and a mutating genome (speed, vision, size, reproduction threshold) where speed and size cost energy, and steer by seeking food, fleeing and finding mates. Populations should oscillate like Lotka–Volterra and trait histograms should show selection. The player is a park ranger with limited actions per season (introduce a species, cull, plant, build a fence, start a controlled burn) and must keep biodiversity within target bands through droughts and disease. Include population charts, inspect-a-creature with lineage, fast-forward thousands of ticks without rendering, and scenario goals (reintroduce wolves without collapse).
prompts.watchFor: Populations crashing in seconds; mutations with no fitness effect; O(n²) neighbour search; fast-forward still rendering every tick; no player objectives.

prompts.title: Formicarium — Ant Colony Game
prompts.prompt: Build an ant colony game as a multi-file web game (index.html + JS + CSS + README). Thousands of ants forage using to-home and to-food pheromone grids that evaporate and diffuse; ants steer with three forward sensors, giving emergent shortest-path trails. The player is the colony's queen-mind: set the worker/soldier/nurse caste ratio, dig tunnels in a side-view nest, place pheromone markers to direct foraging, and expand the nest to grow the brood. A rival red colony competes for food and raids. Overlays show each pheromone map. Win by eliminating the rival or reaching a population target across seasons; starving the colony or losing the queen is defeat.
prompts.watchFor: Ants that know where food is; trails that never evaporate; per-frame allocations killing performance; ants walking through walls; no competition or goals.

prompts.title: Gridlock — Traffic Engineer Game
prompts.prompt: Build a traffic-engineering puzzle game as a multi-file web game (index.html + JS + CSS + README). Vehicles use the Intelligent Driver Model for car-following and MOBIL for lane changes. Each level is a road network with demand from entry points and a throughput target: the player edits light phase timings, adds lanes, turn restrictions, roundabouts, ramp meters and bus lanes within a budget, then runs rush hour and is scored on average delay and throughput. Include a phantom-jam ring road tutorial where tapping a car makes it brake, a motorway merge level and a city junction level. Show a time-space diagram, a flow/density fundamental diagram and star ratings per level.
prompts.watchFor: Cars passing through each other; IDM acceleration blowing up at zero gap; lane changes ignoring followers; identical perfect drivers so jams never form; levels with no failure.

prompts.title: Radar Control — Air Traffic Game
prompts.prompt: Build an air traffic control game as a multi-file web game (index.html + JS + CSS + README) with a green-on-black radar scope: rotating sweep, range rings, runways, waypoints and fading history trails. Aircraft enter with callsign, type, altitude and destination (one of two runways or an exit fix). Select an aircraft to issue heading, altitude and speed changes or clearance to land; aircraft turn at a realistic rate the shorter way, climb and descend gradually, and pilots read back in a text log. Enforce 3 nm / 1000 ft separation with conflict alerts, fuel limits and go-arounds. Traffic ramps up over a shift; score landed and handed-off flights; a loss of separation ends the shift.
prompts.watchFor: Instant heading changes; turns always the same direction; separation checked only laterally; landings allowed from any heading; no escalation.

prompts.title: Orbit — Rocketry Game
prompts.prompt: Build a rocketry game as a multi-file web game (index.html + JS + CSS + README). Design rockets by stacking stages (thrust, Isp, fuel and dry mass) with Tsiolkovsky delta-v per stage, and a budget per mission. Launch through an atmosphere with thinning drag and a player-flown gravity turn, integrate with velocity Verlet or RK4, and draw the predicted conic orbit with apoapsis/periapsis. Support staging, throttle, time warp (disabled in atmosphere), prograde/retrograde burns and a moon with sphere-of-influence switching. HUD: altitude, velocity, dynamic pressure, remaining delta-v, heading indicator. Campaign of contracts (sub-orbital hop, orbit, satellite deployment, lunar flyby, lunar landing) whose rewards unlock parts.
prompts.watchFor: Euler integration spiralling orbits; delta-v ignoring staging; time warp breaking physics; predicted and actual paths disagreeing; drag in vacuum.

prompts.title: Blackout — Grid Operator Game
prompts.prompt: Build a power-grid control-room game as a multi-file web game (index.html + JS + CSS + README). Demand follows a daily curve with weather and TV-pickup surges; supply comes from nuclear, coal, gas CCGT, peakers and hydro with ramp rates and start-up times, plus forecast-dependent wind and solar, and batteries. The player commits and dispatches units; system frequency around 50 Hz moves with supply/demand mismatch scaled by inertia, and falling past thresholds triggers load shedding, then blackout. Track cost, CO₂ and reliability with a stacked generation chart, frequency trace and plant map. Scenario days (winter peak, windless week, heatwave, plant trip) with goals, plus a decade campaign where the player chooses what to build to hit a net-zero target without blackouts.
prompts.watchFor: Frequency ignoring inertia; instant ramping; solar at night; stacked chart not summing to demand; no penalty for over-generation.

prompts.title: Four Hours — Emergency Department Game
prompts.prompt: Build a hospital emergency department management game as a multi-file web game (index.html + JS + CSS + README). Patients arrive by walk-in and ambulance following a time-of-day Poisson rate, are triaged into five acuity levels, and flow through waiting room, cubicles, resus, imaging, and discharge or admission to wards with limited beds that back up the department. The player rosters doctors and nurses with fatigue, opens escalation areas and diverts ambulances at a cost. Show animated patients moving between zones and metrics for 4-hour compliance, waits by acuity, left-without-being-seen and ambulance handover delays. A week-long shift campaign with a major-incident day, seeded RNG so a plan can be replayed fairly, and a final CQC-style rating.
prompts.watchFor: Constant arrival rate; acuity ignored in queues; beds freeing instantly; no seed; fatigue with no effect.

prompts.title: Evolving Walkers
prompts.prompt: Build an evolution game as a multi-file web game (index.html + JS + CSS + README). Creatures made of nodes and rhythmically contracting muscles walk on 2D terrain under fixed-timestep soft-body physics. Generations of 100 are simulated headlessly (ideally in a Web Worker), scored by centre-of-mass distance, and the best reproduce with parameter and structural mutations. The player acts as breeder: choose which creatures survive, design the terrain challenge (hills, stairs, water, obstacles), and compete in time-limited challenges (reach 50 m, climb a hill) against a par generation count. Show the champion replay, fitness charts, species diversity and an ancestor gallery; save/load populations.
prompts.watchFor: Frame-rate-dependent physics; creatures exploiting explosions; mutations leaving floating nodes; fitness from the start node; UI freezing during generations.

prompts.title: Harvest Seasons — Farm Game
prompts.prompt: Build a farm management game as a multi-file web game (index.html + JS + CSS + README) with a top-down tiled farm. Crops have planting windows, visible growth stages, water and nitrogen needs, and yields affected by soil quality that depletes and recovers through rotation, fallow and fertiliser. Daily weather brings rain, frost and drought; irrigation costs money. Add livestock, equipment that speeds field work, hired labour, and a commodity market with supply/demand pricing so storing and selling timing matters. Show a calendar, cash-flow chart, soil-health overlay and year-end accounts. Goal: pay off the farm's mortgage within ten years; missing a payment loses the farm.
prompts.watchFor: Weather- and soil-independent growth; no depletion so monoculture is free; random prices; seasons that don't constrain planting; no loan pressure.

prompts.title: Island Nation — Economy Game
prompts.prompt: Build an agent-based economy game as a multi-file web game (index.html + JS + CSS + README) for a small island nation. Households supply labour, consume and save; firms hire, set prices and wages from inventory and demand, invest and go bankrupt; a bank lends and creates money with stock-flow-consistent accounting. The player is finance minister: set income and corporation tax, spending, minimum wage and tariffs, and trade at a floating exchange rate. Show GDP, unemployment, inflation, Gini and a Lorenz curve, government debt, and a firm size/profit scatter. Elections every four years depend on unemployment, inflation and inequality; shocks (tourism collapse, commodity boom) test the player. Win by serving three terms; a debt crisis or losing an election ends the game.
prompts.watchFor: Money created or destroyed without accounting; random pricing; Gini on an unsorted list; negative unemployment; sliders that change aggregates directly.

prompts.title: Storm Front — Weather Forecaster Game
prompts.prompt: Build a weather forecasting game as a multi-file web game (index.html + JS + CSS + README) on a 2D map of a coastline with mountains. Run a grid atmosphere model: pressure, temperature, humidity and wind with advection, Coriolis circulation around highs and lows, sea breezes from day/night land–sea contrast, orographic rain with a rain shadow, and clouds forming past dew point. Render wind particles, clouds, rain and isobars from the actual fields. The player is the TV forecaster: each day, study the observations (only a few weather stations, with an optional costly radar and balloon launch), then issue 24/48-hour forecasts for five towns (temperature, rain, wind) and storm warnings. The simulation plays out and scores accuracy; missed severe-weather warnings cost trust, and trust over a season decides whether the player keeps the job.
prompts.watchFor: No Coriolis deflection; no rain shadow; advection blow-up from large timesteps; noise isobars; forecasts scored against something other than the simulated outcome.
